issueContext.title: kubelet periodic node status update should not be aligned
issueContext.body:
### What happened? The default `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` is 10s with 4% jitter. The default `nodeStatusReportFrequency` is 5m. The node status will be updated either there's a change or it has been longer than `nodeStatusReportFrequency` since the previous update. `nodeStatusReportFrequency` https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/55b83c92b3b69cd53d5bf22b8ccff859a005241a/pkg/kubelet/kubelet_node_status.go#L580-L581 The jitter of `nodeStatusUpdateFrequency` won't effectively make the periodic node status update to be spread evenly over the 5-minute window. The node status update requests from thousands of nodes are still sent at almost the same time after a couple of days. It can cause the CPU usage to spike every 5 minutes. The following is the APIServer CPU utilization on 96CPU instances. The cluster has 5k nodes that are added in a short period of time. The cluster is idle without any application workload. The utilization can go up to 64% and go down to 14% just because of these node status update requests. ### What did you expect to happen? I'd expect the node status update requests from kubelet to be spread evenly so that the apiserver won't have a minute that it has to handle the requests from most nodes every 5 minutes. ### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)? Bring up a cluster and add nodes in a short period of time. ### Anything else we need to know? Ref: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/105272/files _No response_ ### Kubernetes version
Cutting edge 1.30 ```console $ kubectl version # paste output here ```
### Cloud provider
EKS
### OS version
```console # On Linux: $ cat /etc/os-release # paste output here $ uname -a #

enrichment.problem: When many nodes start at similar times, their periodic node status updates (sent every nodeStatusReportFrequency, default 5 minutes) become aligned, causing a burst of API server requests that can spike CPU usage and affect cluster performance.
enrichment.affected: Large clusters (thousands of nodes) that rely on the default nodeStatusReportFrequency and experience synchronized node status updates after kubelet restarts or node additions.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now adds a random offset (up to ±50% of the configured nodeStatusReportFrequency) to the first status update after startup, spreading the updates over the interval and smoothing the load on the API server.
enrichment.impact: Reduces API server CPU spikes in large clusters, leading to more stable control‑plane performance and smoother scaling of node count without manual jitter configuration.

feature.description: kube-proxy: Checked whether IPv6 was available on Linux before using it.
feature.author: rikatz
feature.userFacingChange: kube-proxy: Check if IPv6 is available on Linux before using it

issueContext.title: Improve IP protocol detection on kube-proxy
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

As part of the implementation of Dual Stack and also the new nftables backend, kube-proxy now does a validation if IPv4 and IPv6 can be used, for instance https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/88dfcb225d41326113990e87b11137641c121a32/cmd/kube-proxy/app/server_linux.go#L112

The improvement here is that while kube-proxy does check if IPTables support IPv6 (and nftables is right now hardcoded, but with a pending action), it doesn't really check if IPv4 and IPv6 kernel subsystem are enabled on the operational system.

So before taking the action of checking the filter service support, I would like to propose that we do a check, on Linux, if "/proc/sys/net/ipv4" exists and if "/proc/sys/net/ipv6" exists before moving on to the specific IPtables and nftables checks

One example of the implementation can be found at https://github.com/rikatz/kubernetes/commit/6c72306bf29b30378412fbf90dcc13cc6f3a23c6, tho this implementation doesn't use the filesystem list, but instead the utilsysctl, which may not be ideal in this case

### Why is this needed?

Some very specific Linux distributions don't load all the iptables or nftables modules by default, and also don't have auto load (x_tables) working properly due to restrictions and modifications made to work. 

Some other distributions disable IPv6 during boot time with ipv6.disable=true. Generally disabling IPv6 doesn't mean the IPv6 rules cannot be added, but on some very specific cases that I could't define why, not all IPv6 filter modules are compiled to the kernel and will partially fail during IPv6 apply, blocking kube-proxy to work.

This is more a proposal to be early defensive on these cases

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy assumed IPv6 support on Linux nodes and attempted to configure IPv6 iptables/nftables rules even when the kernel IPv6 subsystem was disabled or the required sysctl paths (/proc/sys/net/ipv6) were missing, causing proxy failures or crashes.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters running kube-proxy on Linux nodes where IPv6 is disabled or kernel modules are not loaded, particularly in dual‑stack deployments.
enrichment.fix: Added a pre‑check in kube-proxy on Linux to verify that the IPv4 and IPv6 sysctl directories exist before proceeding with IPv6‑specific iptables/nftables configuration. If the directories are absent, IPv6 handling is skipped.
enrichment.impact: Prevents kube-proxy start‑up failures and incorrect rule handling on nodes that have IPv6 disabled or lack kernel support, improving reliability for clusters using dual‑stack or IPv6‑only configurations.

feature.userFacingChange: Add support for CEL expressions with escaped names in structured authentication config.  Using `[` for accessing claims or user data is preferred when names contain characters that would need to be escaped.  CEL optionals via `?` can be used in places where `has` cannot be used, i.e. `claims[?"kubernetes.io"]` or `user.extra[?"domain.io/foo"]`.

enrichment.problem: CEL expressions in the structured authentication config could not reference claim or user fields whose names contained characters that required escaping, and optional access (using `?`) was unavailable where `has` couldn't be used.
enrichment.affected: Users authoring structured authentication configurations, especially those with claim or user extra keys containing special characters such as dots or slashes.
enrichment.fix: Added support for escaped field names using bracket syntax (e.g., `claims[?"kubernetes.io"]`) and introduced the optional operator `?` in CEL, allowing safe access to such fields without needing to rename them.
enrichment.impact: Allows users to write authentication policies that directly reference complex claim or extra user keys, simplifying policy authoring and expanding the range of usable identity token formats.

feature.description: Enabled completion for aliases defined in `kubectlrc`.
feature.author: ardaguclu
feature.userFacingChange: Enabling completion for aliases defined in kuberc

enrichment.problem: Shell tab-completion did not work for aliases defined in the user's kubectlrc/kuberc file, preventing users from using Tab to complete those alias commands.
enrichment.affected: Users who set up custom aliases in kubectlrc/kuberc; any workflow that relies on shell completion for those aliases.
enrichment.fix: Adds support in kubectl's completion logic to recognize and expand aliases defined in kubectlrc, enabling standard shell completion for them.
enrichment.impact: Users who define custom kubectl aliases now get functional tab‑completion, reducing typing errors and speeding up command entry.

feature.description: LeaseLocks could now have custom labels that different holders would overwrite when they became the holder of the underlying lease.
feature.author: DerekFrank
feature.userFacingChange: LeaseLocks can now have custom Labels that different holders will overwrite when they become the holder of the underlying lease.

enrichment.problem: LeaseLocks did not support custom labels, preventing leaders from storing or updating metadata on the lease when they became the holder.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or Kubernetes component that relies on LeaseLock for leader election (e.g., controller‑manager, scheduler, custom controllers) can now set and update custom labels on the lease.
enrichment.fix: Added support for custom Labels on LeaseLocks; each new holder overwrites these labels with its own values when it acquires the lease.
enrichment.impact: Controllers and other components that use leader election via LeaseLocks can now attach arbitrary metadata (e.g., version, region, custom identifiers) to the lease, improving observability, debugging, and integration with external systems.

feature.description: The new `dra_resource_claims_in_use` kubelet metrics reported active `ResourceClaims`, overall and by driver.
feature.author: pohly
feature.userFacingChange: The new `dra_resource_claims_in_use` kubelet metrics informs about active ResourceClaims, overall and by driver.

enrichment.problem: Before this change there was no kubelet metric that exposed how many Device Resource Allocation (DRA) ResourceClaims were currently active, either globally or per driver, limiting operators' ability to observe, troubleshoot, and capacity‑plan DRA usage.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use the Device Resource Allocation (DRA) feature and any tooling that relies on kubelet metrics for monitoring.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the `dra_resource_claims_in_use` metric in the kubelet. The metric reports the total number of active ResourceClaims and breaks the count down by driver, allowing it to be scraped by Prometheus or other monitoring systems.
enrichment.impact: Operators and developers can now monitor DRA usage in real time, set alerts on high claim counts, and better understand resource consumption across drivers, improving observability and aiding debugging of DRA‑related workloads.

feature.description: Graduated configurable endpoints for anonymous authentication using the authentication configuration file to stable.
feature.author: vinayakankugoyal
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate configurable endpoints for anonymous authentication using the authentication configuration file to stable.

enrichment.problem: Anonymous authentication could not be selectively enabled or disabled per API endpoint; the behavior was fixed and not configurable, limiting security controls.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that rely on anonymous authentication and need per‑endpoint control, especially those using the authentication config file.
enrichment.fix: The configurable anonymous authentication endpoints feature is graduated to stable, allowing users to define which API endpoints accept anonymous requests via the authentication configuration file.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now fine‑tune anonymous access, reducing unintended exposure and improving security posture while using a stable, officially supported API.

feature.description: kubelet: Extended the `--image-credential-provider-config` flag to accept a directory path in addition to a single file. When a directory was specified, all .json, .yaml, and .yml files in that directory were loaded and merged in lexicographical order.
feature.author: dims
feature.userFacingChange: kubelet: the `--image-credential-provider-config` flag previously only accepted an individual file, but can now specify a directory path as well; when a directory is specified, all .json/.yaml/.yml files in the directory are loaded and merged in lexicographical order.

enrichment.problem: The `--image-credential-provider-config` flag only accepted a single file, making it cumbersome to manage multiple image credential provider configurations.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet users who configure image credential providers, especially those needing multiple provider definitions.
enrichment.fix: The flag now also accepts a directory path. When a directory is provided, kubelet loads all `.json`, `.yaml`, and `.yml` files in lexicographical order and merges them into a single configuration.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can organize credential provider settings across multiple files or generate them separately. This simplifies configuration management and reduces the risk of editing a single large file.

feature.description: kubeadm: Added support for ECDSA-P384 as an encryption algorithm type in v1beta4.
feature.author: lalitc375
feature.userFacingChange: kubeadm: add support for ECDSA-P384 as an encryption algorithm type in v1beta4.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm could not generate or use ECDSA-P384 certificates, limiting users to other algorithms (e.g., RSA or ECDSA-P256) and preventing compliance with policies that require the stronger P384 curve.
enrichment.affected: Users initializing or joining clusters with kubeadm who need or prefer ECDSA-P384 certificates.
enrichment.fix: Added ECDSA-P384 as a supported encryption algorithm type in the kubeadm v1beta4 configuration, enabling kubeadm to generate and sign certificates with the P384 curve.
enrichment.impact: Clusters bootstrapped with kubeadm can now use stronger ECDSA-P384 TLS certificates, improving security and meeting stricter compliance requirements without needing external tooling.

feature.description: Static pods that reference API objects were denied admission by the kubelet so that static pods would not be silently running even after the mirror pod creation failed.
feature.author: sreeram-venkitesh
feature.userFacingChange:
Static pods that reference API objects are now denied admission by the kubelet so that static pods would not be silently running even after the mirror pod creation fails.
ACTION REQUIRED: Prior to upgrade, ensure static pods are not referencing API objects such as ServiceAccounts, ConfigMaps, Secrets, ResourceClaims, CSIDrivers, PersistentVolumeClaims, or ClusterTrustBundles.

issueContext.title: Kubelet should enforce that static pods do not reference other API objects
issueContext.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
I put into `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/` one defining a static pod with a `serviceAccount`, because I was wondering if this is supported (the documentation does not say, see https://github.com/kubernetes/website/issues/28611#issuecomment-876537379).  The kubelet created the pod but without giving it the relevant mount.  The kubelet did _not_ create the corresponding mirror pod.

Here is the manifest I created:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: test5
spec:
  containers:
  - name: bb
    image: busybox
    command:
    - sleep
    - "864001"
  serviceAccountName: default
```
Here are some relevant log entries from the kubelet:
```
Jul 08 15:55:05 init1 kubelet[4229]: I0708 15:55:05.335792    4229 kubelet.go:1681] "Creating a mirror pod for static pod" pod="default/test5-init1"

Jul 08 15:55:05 init1 kubelet[4229]: E0708 15:55:05.343771    4229 kubelet.go:1683] "Failed creating a mirror pod for" err="pods \"test5-init1\" is forbidden: a mirror pod may not reference service accounts" pod="default/test5-init1"
```

#### What you expected to happen:
I expected consistent treatment --- real pod and mirror pod both exist or both do not exist.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):
I think the above is pretty minimal.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
  ```
  Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"21", GitVersion:"v1.21.1", GitCommit:"5e58841cce77d4bc13713ad2b91fa0d961e69192", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2021-05-12T14:18:45Z", GoVersion:"go1.16.4", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"linux/amd64"}
   Server Version: version.Inf

enrichment.problem: Static pods that reference API objects (e.g., ServiceAccounts, ConfigMaps, Secrets, ResourceClaims, CSIDrivers, PersistentVolumeClaims, ClusterTrustBundles) were admitted by the kubelet even though the creation of the corresponding mirror pod failed, causing the static pod to run silently without required resources.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using static pod manifests that reference API objects such as ServiceAccounts, ConfigMaps, Secrets, ResourceClaims, CSIDrivers, PVCs, or ClusterTrustBundles.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now rejects admission of static pods that reference any API objects. Admission is denied early, preventing the pod from being started when mirror pod creation would fail.
enrichment.impact: Prevents silent, partially functional static pods and ensures consistency between static pods and their mirror pods. Users must update static pod manifests to remove references to API objects before upgrading.

feature.description: Added alpha metrics for compatibility versioning
feature.author: michaelasp

issueContext.title: [Compatibility Version] AddMetrics for effective versions in componentGlobalsRegistry
issueContext.body:
We would like to record the `BinaryVersion`, `EmulationVersion` and `MinCompatibilityVersion` for all components in `componentGlobalsRegistry` used by `kube-apiserver`, `kube-scheduler`, and `kube-controller-manager`.

Implementation can be similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a02806d8cd5efbedb886285a314bd569b2fc828f/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/featuregate/feature_gate.go#L666: 
1. Add a `AddMetrics` method in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/a02806d8cd5efbedb886285a314bd569b2fc828f/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/compatibility/registry.go#L62
2. record the versions in a Gauge metrics with `StabilityLevel: k8smetrics.ALPHA`, in the form of `version_info {component: kube, binary: 1.33, emulation: 1.32, min_compat:1.32} : 1`
3. add the metrics in `kube-apiserver`, `kube-scheduler`, and `kube-controller-manager`.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager) did not expose metrics for their binary, emulation, and minimum compatibility versions, limiting observability of version compatibility across the control plane.
enrichment.affected: Control‑plane components – kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, and kube-controller-manager – and any tooling that relies on version metrics for observability or upgrade validation.
enrichment.fix: Introduced an AddMetrics method in the component compatibility registry and a new alpha gauge metric `version_info` that records BinaryVersion, EmulationVersion, and MinCompatibilityVersion for each component. The metric is registered in kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, and kube-controller-manager.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now monitor and alert on version compatibility information, aiding debugging, upgrade planning, and ensuring components meet required compatibility guarantees.

enrichment.problem: kubeadm init aborts with a SystemVerification pre‑flight error because the Linux kernel version check is treated as a fatal error, causing cluster initialization to fail on supported kernels such as the CentOS 9 kernel 5.14.x.
enrichment.affected: Any user running `kubeadm init` on nodes whose kernel version fails the strict validation check, notably CentOS/RHEL 9 and similar distributions.
enrichment.fix: The validation logic for the Linux kernel version was changed to emit a warning instead of an error, allowing the init process to continue even when the kernel version does not exactly match the expected range.
enrichment.impact: Users can now initialize clusters with kubeadm on systems that have newer or non‑standard kernel versions (e.g., CentOS, RHEL, ppc64le) without needing to downgrade or apply work‑arounds, reducing false‑positive pre‑flight failures and improving overall compatibility.

feature.description: Built Kubernetes using Go 1.24.3.
feature.author: cpanato
feature.userFacingChange: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.3

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes source was built with an older Go compiler, which could lead to build failures, missing compiler bug fixes, and lack of recent security updates for developers compiling the code.
enrichment.affected: Developers and CI systems that compile Kubernetes from source, as well as downstream distribution maintainers.
enrichment.fix: The build system has been updated to require and use Go 1.24.3 for compiling Kubernetes.
enrichment.impact: Improves build reliability and security for anyone building Kubernetes from source (developers, CI pipelines, distribution packagers). No change to runtime behavior for clusters.

feature.description: Graduated scheduler `QueueingHint` support to GA (general availability)
feature.author: sanposhiho

enrichment.problem: The QueueingHint feature in the scheduler was previously in beta, requiring explicit enablement and lacking GA guarantees, limiting its use in production environments.
enrichment.affected: Users who want stable, production‑ready QueueingHint support for pod scheduling.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler's QueueingHint support has been graduated to General Availability, making the feature stable, enabled by default, and covered by the standard support policy.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now reliably use QueueingHint for more efficient pod queuing and placement without extra configuration, enabling production workloads to benefit from improved scheduling behavior.

feature.description: Graduated `ResilientWatchCacheInitialization` to GA.
feature.author: serathius
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate ResilientWatchCacheInitialization to GA

enrichment.problem: The ResilientWatchCacheInitialization feature, which makes watch cache initialization more reliable, was only available in alpha/beta and required a feature gate, limiting its production use.
enrichment.affected: Users of the Kubernetes API server watch mechanism, especially those running production workloads that depend on continuous watch streams.
enrichment.fix: The feature has been graduated to GA, removing the feature gate and guaranteeing stability and support for production clusters.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now rely on stable, resilient watch cache initialization without extra configuration, improving watch reliability and reducing disruptions for workloads that depend on watch streams.

feature.description:
kubeadm: graduated the `NodeLocalCRISocket` feature gate to beta and enabed it by default. When its enabled, kubeadm will:
  1. Generate a `/var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml` file to customize the `containerRuntimeEndpoint` field in per-node kubelet configurations.
  2. Remove the `kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket` annotation from nodes during upgrade operations.
  3. Remove the `--container-runtime-endpoint` flag from the `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env` file during upgrades.
feature.author: HirazawaUi
feature.userFacingChange:
kubeadm: graduated the `NodeLocalCRISocket` feature gate to beta and enabed it by default. When its enabled, kubeadm will:
  1. Generate a `/var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml` file to customize the `containerRuntimeEndpoint` field in per-node kubelet configurations.
  2. Remove the `kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket` annotation from nodes during upgrade operations.
  3. Remove the `--container-runtime-endpoint` flag from the `/var/lib/kubelet/kubeadm-flags.env` file during upgrades.

enrichment.problem: Clusters using kubeadm relied on the deprecated kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket annotation and the --container-runtime-endpoint flag to set a per‑node CRI socket. Upgrades required manual cleanup and there was no standard per‑node kubelet configuration file for this setting.
enrichment.affected: All kubeadm‑provisioned clusters, especially those that previously used the kubeadm.alpha.kubernetes.io/cri-socket annotation or the --container-runtime-endpoint flag to customize the CRI socket on nodes.
enrichment.fix: The NodeLocalCRISocket feature gate is graduated to beta and enabled by default. kubeadm now automatically creates /var/lib/kubelet/instance-config.yaml to set the containerRuntimeEndpoint field, and during upgrades it removes the old annotation and the --container-runtime-endpoint flag from the node's kubelet configuration.
enrichment.impact: Users no longer need to manage legacy annotations or flags for CRI socket configuration. The process becomes automated and consistent across upgrades, reducing operational friction and preventing configuration drift.

feature.description:
Graduated relaxed DNS search string validation to GA. For the Pod API, `.spec.dnsConfig.searches`
now allows an underscore (`_`) where a dash (`-`) would be allowed, and it allows search strings be a single dot `.`.
feature.author: adrianmoisey
feature.userFacingChange:
Graduated relaxed DNS search string validation to GA. For the Pod API, `.spec.dnsConfig.searches`
now allows an underscore (`_`) where a dash (`-`) would be allowed, and it allows search strings be a single dot `.`.

enrichment.problem: The Pod spec validation for .spec.dnsConfig.searches was overly strict, rejecting DNS search strings that contained an underscore (_) or were a single dot (.). This prevented users from configuring pods with such DNS search entries.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or updating Pods with .spec.dnsConfig.searches containing '_' or '.' strings; clusters that need custom DNS search domain configurations.
enrichment.fix: The validation logic has been relaxed and graduated to GA. The API now accepts underscores in search strings where dashes were previously allowed, and it also permits a single dot as a valid search string.
enrichment.impact: Admins can now use broader DNS search configurations, including legacy or custom setups that require underscores or a solitary dot, without pod creation failures. This improves compatibility and flexibility for workloads relying on specific DNS naming conventions.

feature.description: DRA kubelet: Fixed the kubelet to also clean up `ResourceSlices` in some additional failure scenarios (driver was removed forcibly or crashed and did not restart).
feature.author: pohly
feature.userFacingChange: DRA kubelet: the kubelet now also cleans up ResourceSlices in some additional failure scenarios (driver gets removed forcibly or crashes and does not restart).

issueContext.title: DRA: detect stale DRA plugin sockets
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

@klueska observed that after uninstalling his DRA driver *without* removing the Unix Domain socket used for gRPC towards the kubelet, kubelet didn't unregister the driver. We may have to add some liveness probing to `pkg/kubelet/cm/dra/plugin/registration.go`.

/sign node
/wg device-management
/priority backlog

### Why is this needed?

The kubelet needs to remove ResourceSlices on behalf of a defunct DRA driver.

enrichment.problem: When a DRA driver was forcibly removed or crashed without restarting, the kubelet failed to clean up the driver’s ResourceSlices, leaving stale resource allocations in the cluster.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using Device Resource Allocation (DRA) drivers; specifically when a driver is removed forcibly or crashes and does not restart, leading to stale ResourceSlices.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now detects these failure scenarios and automatically deletes the orphaned ResourceSlices, ensuring the driver’s resources are fully unregistered.
enrichment.impact: Prevents resource leakage and stale resource information that could mislead scheduling and resource accounting, improving cluster stability for workloads that rely on DRA drivers.

feature.description: Graduated the `WinDSR` feature in the kube-proxy to GA. The `WinDSR` feature gate was enabled by default.
feature.author: rzlink
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate the WinDSR feature in the kube-proxy to GA. The `WinDSR` feature gate is now enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: The WinDSR (Windows Direct Server Return) feature was previously behind a feature gate and required explicit enablement, preventing default use of direct server return traffic handling in kube-proxy on Windows nodes.
enrichment.affected: Kubernetes clusters that run Windows nodes and use kube-proxy for service routing.
enrichment.fix: The WinDSR feature gate is graduated to GA and enabled by default in kube-proxy, making DSR functionality automatically available on Windows clusters.
enrichment.impact: Clusters with Windows nodes no longer need to manually enable the WinDSR gate; workloads that benefit from direct server return (e.g., high‑performance load‑balancing) will see improved traffic handling out of the box.

feature.description:
The PreferSameTrafficDistribution feature gate is now enabled by default,
enabling the `PreferSameNode` traffic distribution value for Services.
feature.author: danwinship
feature.userFacingChange:
The PreferSameTrafficDistribution feature gate is now enabled by default,
enabling the `PreferSameNode` traffic distribution value for Services.

enrichment.problem: The PreferSameTrafficDistribution feature gate was disabled by default, so the `PreferSameNode` traffic distribution option for Services could not be used, limiting control over intra-node traffic routing.
enrichment.affected: Users of Services who want same‑node traffic routing and any workloads that rely on Service load‑balancing; cluster administrators notice a default behavior change.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is now enabled by default, activating the `PreferSameNode` traffic distribution value for Services. No manual gate activation is required.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now prefer routing Service traffic to pods on the same node as the client, reducing network hop latency and bandwidth usage. Existing workloads see a change in load‑balancing behavior that may improve performance or affect distribution balance.

feature.description: Promoted the Ordered Namespace Deletion test to Conformance.
feature.author: BenTheElder
feature.userFacingChange: Promote Ordered Namespace Deletion to Conformance

issueContext.title: Promote Ordered Namespace Deletion Tests to Conformance
issueContext.body:
If we're advertising this as a security fix going GA (in v1.34 #131514) then as a user I'd want confidence that this is standard and nobody has patched it to break the security mitigation it provides. I think we should promote this test to conformance.

I worry if we don't that we provide a false sense of closing the gap that led to this KEP (a CVE with network policy potentially being deleted before workloads fundamentally leaving an exploitable enforcement gap across implementations of network policy #126587)

There was a flakiness issue from another unrelated test making the namespace controller have high load, a patch for that is in flight (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131518), but later when we have proven the test stable, I think we should be looking at this behavior in-scope.

https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/5080-ordered-namespace-deletion/README.md#design-details
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/5080

Specifically this ensures that pods are deleted and waited on before other resources.
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/5080-ordered-namespace-deletion/README.md#deletionorderpriority-mechanism

/milestone v1.34
/sig architecture api-machinery
/area conformance
cc @dims @johnbelamaric @cici37 

details above pulled from: https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C5P3FE08M/p1745939545014909 (#sig-architecture in https://slack.k8s.io)

enrichment.problem: The conformance test suite did not require implementations to enforce ordered namespace deletion, so clusters could delete non-pod resources before pods, potentially leaving a brief security gap (e.g., network policies being removed while pods still ran).
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters that support conformance testing; any workloads that rely on namespaces being deleted in a safe, ordered manner, especially those using network policies or other security mechanisms.
enrichment.fix: The Ordered Namespace Deletion test has been promoted to the conformance suite, making it a mandatory pass for any conformant Kubernetes distribution.

issueContext.title: [Compatibility Version] alphas with emulated version
issueContext.body:
Per the compatibility version KEP, alphas are outside the scope of compatibility version.

https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-architecture/4330-compatibility-versions/README.md#non-goals

> Support --emulation-version for Alpha features. Alpha feature are not designed to be upgradable, so we will not allow alpha features to be enabled when --emulation-version is set.

We current don't have proper safeguards for this.

- [ ] Alpha features should not be permitted to be enabled with emulated version
- [ ] Alpha APIs should not be permitted to be enabled with emulated version

/cc @aaron-prindle @jpbetz 

/triage accepted
/sig architecture
/sig api-machinery

enrichment.problem: Alpha metrics could be enabled while the server is running with --emulation-version, but alpha features are not supported under compatibility emulation, leading to unsupported configurations without any indication.

enrichment.fix: The apiserver now emits a warning when alpha metrics are accessed while an emulated version is set, alerting operators to the unsupported usage.
enrichment.impact: Operators get immediate feedback about the misuse, preventing confusion and encouraging removal of alpha metrics in compatibility mode, which maintains the integrity of version compatibility guarantees.

issueContext.title: In place pod resizing should be designed into the kubelet config state loop, not alongside it
issueContext.body:
### What happened?

#102884 in its alpha state introduces a new challenge to the kubelet state machine - partial and deferred acceptance of spec changes to a pod in the kubelet, while at the same time we are realizing that the kubelet is not properly feeding actual state to  components #116970.

Last minute 1.27 fix #116702 works around but doesn't resolve a key side effect of this problem - reverting the pod state incorrectly / temporarily.  The pod worker receives new state (in an ordered fashion from admission, and before that podManager) and then invokes SyncPod with the "latest".  In-place resizing then mutates podManager directly, and continues its execution with a different syncPod.  However, once we fix #116970, this will be impossible - other components have to consult the pod worker for the latest state, not podManager.

Visually this is described at https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1wbPFANXVbk-e-5BvVHaZScqoqJsfcU_FQVmG-N7pv3c/edit#slide=id.g1de8a1ca1a4_0_1673 (shared with kubernetes-sig-node google group)

To graduate to beta in-place resizing needs a new capability added to the kubelet state machine - the ability to decide when the spec change requested is "acted on" by the kubelet.  There are a couple of ways we could design this, but they need to fit harmoniously into the larger changes we're making to kubelet state vs being working around the kubelet state machine.

To do that we need to make sure we understand the rules that any "level driven update" to pod spec must follow and then implement a mechanism in the kubelet.  This issue covers articulating those rules and getting answers as an input to the change we should make to kubelet admission.

Question:

* What future spec changes to pods have been discussed that would have requirements?
* Can spec changes to a pod be rejected permanently (kubelet never accepts them)?
* When a spec change to a pod is rejected temporarily, what other aspects of the pod spec must be updated?

enrichment.problem: When a node does not have enough free resources to satisfy all pending in-place pod resize requests, the kubelet previously handled the requests in an arbitrary order, causing lower‑priority or BestEffort pods to be resized before higher‑priority or Guaranteed pods, leading to unfair resource allocation and potential disruption of critical workloads.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that use in‑place pod resizing on nodes with limited resources, especially those relying on PriorityClass and QoS to differentiate importance.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now sorts pending resize requests by the pod's PriorityClass and QoS class. Requests from higher‑priority and higher‑QoS pods are processed first, and lower‑priority requests are deferred when node capacity is insufficient.
enrichment.impact: Critical and higher‑priority pods receive resource adjustments before less important pods, improving fairness and reliability of in‑place resizing. Users can rely on priorityClass and QoS semantics to influence resize behavior, reducing unexpected resource contention and pod failures.

feature.description: Added a `container_swap_limit_bytes` metric to expose the swap limit assigned to containers under the `LimitedSwap` swap behavior.
feature.author: iholder101
feature.userFacingChange: Adds a `container_swap_limit_bytes` metric to expose the swap limit assigned to containers under the `LimitedSwap` swap behavior.

issueContext.title: expose calculated swap limit metric for containers
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently, when `LimitedSwap` is enabled, the Kubelet calculates a swap limit for each container. However, this calculated value is not exposed, leaving users with no visibility into this critical resource constraint.

This transparency is needed to effectively monitor swap resource limits and troubleshoot swap-related issues.

I'd like to propose introducting of a new kubelet metric, `container_spec_swap_limit_bytes`, to report the calculated swap limit for each container and be available at the `/metrics/resource` endpoint. 

### Why is this needed?

Exposing this metric would provide much-needed visibility for calculated swap limits per container and align the behavior with other container resource metrics.

enrichment.problem: When the LimitedSwap feature is enabled, the kubelet calculates a per‑container swap limit but does not expose that value, leaving administrators without visibility into this important resource constraint.
enrichment.affected: Node administrators and any workloads that rely on swap limits for performance or stability, because they can now see the swap limit per container via metrics.
enrichment.fix: Introduces a new metric `container_swap_limit_bytes` published by the kubelet on the `/metrics/resource` endpoint, reporting the calculated swap limit for each container under the LimitedSwap behavior.
enrichment.impact: Provides observability into container swap limits, enabling monitoring, alerting, and troubleshooting of swap‑related issues and aligning swap visibility with other resource metrics.

enrichment.impact: Clusters can now obtain more accurate request‑cost metrics for LIST operations, improving API throttling, quota enforcement, and overall API server performance under heavy list workloads.

feature.description: Added HPA support to pod-level resource specifications. When the pod-level resource feature was enabled, HPAs configured with `Resource` type metrics calculated the pod resources from `pod.Spec.Resources` field, if specified.
feature.author: laoj2
feature.userFacingChange: Adds HPA support to pod-level resource specifications. When the pod-level resource feature is enabled, HPAs configured with `Resource` type metrics will calculate the pod resources from `pod.Spec.Resources` field, if specified.

issueContext.title: HPA support for pod-level resource specifications
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

With k8s 1.34, `PodLevelResources` will allow users to specify resources on Pod level instead of on Container level. More info on how this works in the [KEP](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/2837)

This is a placeholder/umbrella issue, similar to VPA's https://github.com/kubernetes/autoscaler/issues/7571

### Why is this needed?

HPA needs to be able to correctly calculate the resources requested by a pod, when it's defined at pod or container level. Today, it calculates the pod requests by aggregating the requests of all containers within a pod: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/988cf21f0975cf95444a619481c13d2503d8ec6a/pkg/controller/podautoscaler/replica_calculator.go#L452-L475

We could use https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/988cf21f0975cf95444a619481c13d2503d8ec6a/staging/src/k8s.io/component-helpers/resource/helpers.go, to calculate the pod requests in HPA.

enrichment.problem: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) could only calculate pod resource requests from container-level specifications, ignoring resources defined at the pod level via the new PodLevelResources feature.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the PodLevelResources feature and HPA configured with Resource metrics; workloads that specify pod-level resources.
enrichment.fix: When the pod-level resource feature is enabled, HPA controllers now read the pod's `pod.Spec.Resources` field for Resource‑type metrics, allowing correct calculation of pod resources defined at the pod level.
enrichment.impact: Autoscaling decisions become accurate for workloads that specify resources at the pod level, preventing mis‑scaling (over‑ or under‑provisioning) and enabling the new PodLevelResources feature to be used with HPA.

feature.description: kube-apiserver: Previously persisted `CustomResourceDefinition` objects with an invalid whitespace-only `caBundle` could serve requests that did not require conversion.
feature.author: tiffanny29631
feature.userFacingChange: kube-apiserver: previously persisted CustomResourceDefinition objects with an invalid whitespace-only `caBundle` can now serve requests that do not require conversion.

issueContext.title: Special-case whitespace-only values in webhook conversion client construction
issueContext.body:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124061#issuecomment-2142880235

Comment from liggitt:

> I think I'd suggest the following:

> 1. For CRDs that do not have an Established=True condition (on CRD creation or pre-serving updates)
a. In validation, allow arbitrary caBundle values like today
b. In staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/controller/establish/establishing_controller.go, gate setting Established=True on the caBundle value being valid (if specified). This means until caBundle is populated with a valid value in a new CRD, the CRD will not be served and will not show up in discovery.

> 2. For CRDs that do have an Established=True condition (which means they are being served)
a. In validation, add ratcheting validation (this PR) so valid caBundle values have to stay valid
b. When constructing the webhook conversion client in webhookClientConfigForCRD, consider special-casing whitespace-only values to treat them as an empty value and fall back to system trust roots. This will still likely fail when attempting to contact the conversion webhook, but reads/writes that don't require conversion could still succeed, so if there were no persisted objects or only requests to the version matching the storage version and all existing persisted objects were in that version, clients like the namespace controller could be unblocked.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/124061 addresses 1a, 1b, 2a.

2b is still pending

enrichment.problem: CRDs that had a whitespace‑only `caBundle` were considered invalid, causing the apiserver to reject even requests that didn’t need webhook conversion. This blocked controllers (e.g., namespace controller) and any workload interacting with such CRDs.
enrichment.affected: CustomResourceDefinition objects that have an Established=True condition and a whitespace‑only `caBundle`; any workloads or controllers using those CRDs.
enrichment.fix: The apiserver now treats a whitespace‑only `caBundle` as an empty value, falling back to the system trust roots when building the conversion webhook client. Requests that do not require conversion can therefore be served successfully.
enrichment.impact: CRDs with a mis‑configured `caBundle` no longer prevent the apiserver from handling non‑conversion API calls, restoring normal operation for controllers and workloads that rely on those CRDs.

feature.description: kubeadm: graduated the kubeadm specific feature gate `WaitForAllControlPlaneComponents` to GA. The feature gate is was locked to always be enabled and on node initialization kubeadm performed a health check for all control plane components and not only the `kube-apiserver`.

feature.description: Graduated the `WatchList` feature gate to beta for kube-apiserver and enabled `WatchListClient` for KCM.

enrichment.problem: The WatchList feature gate was only available in Alpha, requiring manual enablement and lacking the stability guarantees of a beta feature. Controllers could not use the WatchListClient by default.
enrichment.affected: Any Kubernetes cluster running kube-apiserver and kube‑controller‑manager. Controllers that rely on watch streams will see improved behavior.

feature.description: `DRAPrioritizedList` was turned on by default which made it possible to provide a prioritized list of subrequests in a `ResourceClaim`.

feature.description: `kubeadm`: Started using a named port `probe-port` for all probes in the static pod manifests generated by `kubeadm` for the `kube-apiserver`, `kube-controller-manager`, `kube-scheduler`, and related components. feature.description:

feature.description: Enabled compact snapshots in the watch cache based on `etcd` compaction events.

enrichment.problem: The API server’s watch cache did not compact its in‑memory snapshots when etcd performed compaction, causing the cache to retain stale data and potentially grow unbounded, leading to increased memory usage and degraded watch performance.

enrichment.fix: Watch cache now listens to etcd compaction events and creates compact snapshots accordingly, discarding obsolete data and freeing memory.

feature.description: Added the `DetectCacheInconsistency` feature gate, allowing the API server to periodically verify consistency between its `cache` and `etcd`. Detected inconsistencies reported via the `apiserver_storage_consistency_checks_total` metric and trigger purging of affected cache snapshots.
feature.author: serathius
feature.userFacingChange: Add DetectCacheInconsistency feature gate that allows apiserver to periodically compare consistency between cache and etcd. Inconsistency is reported to `apiserver_storage_consistency_checks_total` metric and results in cache snapshots being purged.

enrichment.problem: The kube-apiserver cache could become inconsistent with the source of truth in etcd, causing stale or incorrect data to be served to clients without any detection or alerting.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running the kube-apiserver; any workload or component that reads resources through the API server could be affected by stale data if the cache becomes inconsistent.
enrichment.fix: Introduces the DetectCacheInconsistency feature gate. When enabled, the apiserver periodically compares its in‑memory cache snapshots with etcd, reports any mismatches via the `apiserver_storage_consistency_checks_total` metric, and automatically purges the inconsistent cache snapshots.
enrichment.impact: Provides visibility into cache‑etcd drift and ensures that stale data is not served, improving data correctness and cluster reliability. Operators gain a metric to monitor consistency health and can react faster to storage‑layer issues.

feature.description:

feature.description: Added memory tracking to scheduler performance tests to help detect memory leaks and monitored memory usage patterns while running `scheduler_perf`.
feature.author: utam0k
feature.userFacingChange: Add memory tracking to scheduler performance tests to help detect memory leaks and monitor memory usage patterns while running scheduler_perf

issueContext.title: scheduler_perf: Add Memory Tracking to Detect Memory Leaks
issueContext.body:
## What type of Issue is this?

/kind feature
/sig scheduling

## What this Issue does / why we need it:

This issue proposes adding memory tracking capabilities to `scheduler_perf` to detect memory leaks and regressions before they reach production.

### Background

The Kubernetes scheduler has experienced critical memory leaks in production:

- **#120622**: QHint inFlightPods memory leak
- **#111773**: Preemption strategy memory leak
- **#83895**: Work queue timer memory leak
- And your custom scheduler plugins?

These issues were discovered only after deployment to production, causing a significant operational impact. The variety of root causes (watch operations, preemption logic, queue timers, map cleanup) demonstrates the need for systematic memory tracking.

### Proposed Solution

Add memory tracking to `scheduler_perf` that monitors:

- **HeapMemoryInUse**: Current heap memory usage (MB)
- **GoroutineCount**: Number of active goroutines
- **MemoryGrowthRate**: Rate of memory increase (MB/min)

Frankly, what to monitor is debatable. I welcome your opinion.

PoC is https://github.com/utam0k/kubernetes/tree/scheduler-perf-memory/test/integration/scheduler_perf/memory/demo, and confirm PoC can detect #120622 case.

Here is the summary by PoC:

- **Workload**: 150,000 pods
- **Duration**: ~1.5 minutes

| Metric                     | Baseline    | Memory Leak | Difference         |
| -------------------------- | ----------- | ----------- | ------------------ |
| HeapMemoryInUse (Average)  | 4418 MB     | 4941 MB     | +523 MB (+11.8%)   |
| HeapMemoryInUse (Max)      | 6626 MB     | 7770 MB     | +1144 MB (+17.3%)  |
| MemoryGrowthRate           | 1946 MB/min | 2801 MB/min | +855 MB/min (+44%) |
| GoroutineCount (Average)   | 2,475       | 2,483       | +8 (+0.3%)         |
| GoroutineCount (Max)       | 3,015       | 3,221       | +206 (+6.8%)       |

enrichment.problem: Scheduler performance tests (scheduler_perf) lacked built‑in memory usage tracking, making it difficult to detect memory leaks or abnormal memory growth before code reached production.
enrichment.affected: Teams running scheduler_perf (e.g., scheduler developers, plugin authors, CI systems) who need visibility into scheduler memory behavior.
enrichment.fix: Added memory tracking to scheduler_perf. The test now records HeapMemoryInUse, GoroutineCount, and MemoryGrowthRate, exposing these metrics during runs so leaks can be identified and trends monitored.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines can now catch scheduler memory regressions early, reducing risk of production‑level memory leaks and improving overall scheduler reliability.

feature.description: Graduated `PodObservedGenerationTracking` feature to beta and had it on by default. This feature meant that the top level `status.observedGeneration` and `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` fields in Pods were populated to reflect the `metadata.generation` of the podspec at the time that the status or condition was reported.
feature.author: natasha41575
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate `PodObservedGenerationTracking` feature to beta and have it on by default. This feature means that the top level `status.observedGeneration` and `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` fields in pods will now be populated to reflect the `metadata.generation` of the podspec at the time that the status or condition is being reported.

enrichment.problem: Pod status fields `status.observedGeneration` and `status.conditions[].observedGeneration` were left empty, making it difficult for users and controllers to determine which pod spec generation a given status or condition corresponded to.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that inspects Pod status or condition fields—e.g., operators, monitoring tools, and custom controllers—will now see accurate observedGeneration values.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the `PodObservedGenerationTracking` feature to beta and enabled it by default. The kube-apiserver now populates the top‑level `status.observedGeneration` and each condition’s `observedGeneration` with the pod’s `metadata.generation` at the time the status or condition is reported.
enrichment.impact: Operators, tooling, and custom controllers can reliably correlate pod status and condition updates with the exact pod spec generation, improving debugging, observability, and correctness of decision‑making logic that depends on pod spec changes.

feature.description: Added the `SizeBasedListCostEstimate` feature gate (enabled by default), which changes how APF seats are assigned to `LIST` requests. With this feature, one seat is assigned per 100KB of data loaded into memory at once during a `LIST` operation.
feature.author: serathius
feature.userFacingChange: Add SizeBasedListCostEstimate feature gate, enabled by default, changing method of assigning APF seats to LIST request. Assign one seat per 100KB of data loaded to memory at once to handle LIST request.

enrichment.problem: API Priority and Fairness (APF) assigned a fixed seat cost for LIST requests, ignoring the amount of data returned. Large LIST operations could consume a single seat while loading a lot of data, leading to unfair API server resource distribution and potential performance degradation for other clients.
enrichment.affected: Clients that perform large LIST operations (e.g., controllers, kubectl, custom controllers) and the API server handling those requests.
enrichment.fix: Introduce the SizeBasedListCostEstimate feature gate (enabled by default). APF now estimates the cost of a LIST request based on the size of data loaded into memory, assigning one seat for each 100KB of data processed during the LIST operation.
enrichment.impact: Makes APF seat allocation proportional to actual resource usage, preventing large LIST calls from monopolizing API server capacity. This improves fairness and stability of API traffic, especially for clusters with heavy list-intensive workloads.

feature.description: Kubelet detected terminal CSI volume mount failures due to exceeded attachment limits on the node and marked the Stateful Pod as Failed, allowing its controller to recreate it. This prevented Pods from getting stuck indefinitely in the `ContainerCreating` state.
feature.author: torredil
feature.userFacingChange: Kubelet now detects terminal CSI volume mount failures due to exceeded attachment limits on the node and marks the stateful pod as Failed, allowing its controller to recreate it. This prevents pods from getting stuck indefinitely in the `ContainerCreating` state.

enrichment.problem: When a node reached its CSI volume attachment limit, kubelet treated the resulting terminal volume mount failures as non‑fatal and left the stateful pod in the ContainerCreating phase, causing the pod to remain stuck indefinitely.
enrichment.affected: StatefulSet pods (and other stateful workloads) on nodes where the CSI volume attachment limit is exceeded.
enrichment.fix: Kubelet now detects terminal CSI volume mount failures that are caused by exceeded attachment limits and marks the affected stateful pod as Failed. This allows the owning controller (e.g., StatefulSet) to recreate the pod.
enrichment.impact: Pods are no longer stuck forever in ContainerCreating, reducing downtime and manual intervention for stateful workloads that hit volume attachment limits.

issueContext.title: Unify how metric reference resources
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added? There are just to many ways metric reference resources, labels include different contents causing confusion and making filtering hard and joining impossible. Example metrics collected on a empty kind cluster by running `kubectl get --raw /metrics | grep -i apiservice`, it is not exhaustive: * [recommended] `{group="$GROUP", resource="$RESOURCE"}` for example: `{group="apiregistration.k8s.io",resource="apiservices"}`
Metric Stability Example time series
apiserver_longrunning_requests STABLE {component="apiserver",group="apiregistration.k8s.io",resource="apiservices",scope="cluster",subresource="",verb="WATCH",version="v1"}
apiserver_request_duration_seconds STABLE {component="apiserver",dry_run="",group="apiregistration.k8s.io",resource="apiservices",scope="resource",subresource="",verb="POST",version="v1"}
apiserver_request_sli_duration_seconds ALPHA {component="apiserver",group="apiregistration.k8s.io",resource="apiservices",scope="resource",subresource="",verb="POST",version="v1"}
apiserver_request_total STABLE {code="201",component="apiserver",dry_run="",group="apiregistration.k8s.io",resource="apiservices",scope="resource",subresource="",verb="POST",version="v1"} 20
apiserver_response_sizes STABLE {component="apiserver",group="apiregistration.k8s.io",resource="apiservices",scope="cluster",subresource="",verb="WATCH",version="v1"}
* Resource_prefix=”/${GROUP}/${RESOURCE}”, for example `{resource_prefix"/apiregistration.k8s.io/apiservices"}`
Metric Stability Example time series

enrichment.problem: The apiserver_storage_objects metric used inconsistent label conventions compared to other apiserver metrics, making filtering, aggregation, and joining difficult for users monitoring Kubernetes API server behavior.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that scrape the apiserver metrics, especially those using the deprecated apiserver_storage_objects metric in dashboards or alerts.
enrichment.fix: The metric is deprecated and replaced by apiserver_resource_objects, which uses a unified label set (e.g., group, resource, scope) consistent with the rest of the apiserver metrics.
enrichment.impact: Users and tooling that rely on API server metrics (e.g., Prometheus dashboards, alerts) can now query and correlate data across metrics more reliably, reducing confusion and simplifying observability configurations.

feature.description: Memory limits could be decreased with a `NotRequired` resize restart policy. When decreasing memory limits,a best-effort check was performed to prevent limits from decreasing below usage and triggering an OOM-kill.
feature.author: tallclair

issueContext.title: [FG:InPlacePodVerticalScaling] Enable memory limit decrease
issueContext.body:
/kind bug

When shrinking the pod-level memory limits (sum of container limits iff all containers have limits), the Kubelet checks the current pod memory usage, and doesn't apply the new limits if the new limits < current usage. However, the Kubelet doesn't place the same restriction on containers, and we don't require container runtimes to make the same check.

In practice, this means that for a single container pod, decreasing the memory limit below usage will result in the resize being indefinitely in progress, but for a multiple container pod, if some containers have sufficient free memory, you can shrink the memory limits below usage for a container in the pod, resulting in that container being OOM-killed.

What is the desired behavior here?

https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cEFLXKwNOSNLAkzyhoJUgkBW0OiX-9bXB_aJV7OAypw/edit?tab=t.0 provides more background information and several options for how this should be handled.

/sig node
/priority important-soon

enrichment.problem: When decreasing pod memory limits using InPlacePodVerticalScaling with a NotRequired restart policy, the kubelet only checked pod‑level usage. Container‑level limits could be set below current usage, causing the resize to hang or the container to be OOM‑killed, especially in multi‑container pods.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use InPlacePodVerticalScaling (NotRequired restart policy) and containers whose memory usage exceeds the proposed lower limit were at risk of OOM kills or stalled resize operations.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now performs a best‑effort check against current memory usage before applying a decreased memory limit. If the new limit would be lower than usage, the limit reduction is prevented, avoiding inadvertent OOM kills.
enrichment.impact: Users can safely decrease memory limits during vertical scaling without risking unexpected OOM termination of containers, improving reliability of in‑place pod vertical scaling operations.

feature.description: kubelet reported a hash of the credential provider configuration via the `kubelet_credential_provider_config_info` metric. The hash was exposed in the `hash` label.

enrichment.impact: Admins can now reliably detect configuration changes via Prometheus/metrics, enabling better observability, troubleshooting, and security auditing of credential provider updates.

feature.description: Eliminated work when creating Services or understanding port purposes, especially for external resources deployed via Helm charts.
feature.author: rushmash91

enrichment.problem: Creating Services required manual effort to determine and specify port purposes, causing confusion and extra work, particularly when dealing with external resources deployed via Helm charts.
enrichment.affected: Users who create Services with kubectl, especially those deploying external resources through Helm charts.
enrichment.fix: The change removes the need for that manual work by simplifying Service creation and clarifying port handling, so users no longer have to infer or specify ports for external resources.
enrichment.impact: Reduces time and potential errors for developers and operators when creating Services, improving the Helm chart development experience and overall CLI usability.

feature.description:
If `PreBindPreFlight` returned `Skip`, the scheduler didn't run the plugin at `PreBind`.
If any `PreBindPreFlight` returned `Success`, the scheduler put NominatedNodeName to the pod 
so that other components (such as the cluster autoscaler) could notice the pod was going to be bound to the node.
feature.author: sanposhiho
feature.userFacingChange:
If PreBindPreFlight returns Skip, the scheduler doesn't run the plugin at PreBind.
If any PreBindPreFlight returns Success, the scheduler puts NominatedNodeName to the pod 
so that other components (such as the cluster autoscaler) can notice the pod is going to be bound to the node.

issueContext.title: KEP-5278: Put NNN based on `PreBindPreFlight`

enrichment.problem: The scheduler ignored PreBindPreFlight results: when a plugin returned Skip, it still ran at PreBind, and when any PreBindPreFlight returned Success, the scheduler did not set the pod's NominatedNodeName, preventing components like the cluster autoscaler from seeing the pending binding.
enrichment.affected: Pods being scheduled that use PreBindPreFlight-enabled plugins; cluster autoscaler and similar components that rely on NominatedNodeName.
enrichment.fix: Updated kube-scheduler logic to (1) skip executing a plugin at the PreBind stage if its PreBindPreFlight returned Skip, and (2) set NominatedNodeName on the pod when any PreBindPreFlight returns Success, enabling other components to detect the intended binding.
enrichment.impact: Ensures correct interaction between the scheduler and components such as the cluster autoscaler, improving pod placement decisions and preventing missed scaling signals.

feature.description: Increased APF max seats to 100 for LIST requests.
feature.author: serathius
feature.userFacingChange: Increase APF max seats to 100 for LIST requests

enrichment.problem: The default API Priority and Fairness (APF) max seats for LIST requests was low, leading to excessive throttling of large or many concurrent LIST calls, which could degrade performance for clients that list resources frequently.
enrichment.affected: Any workload or user that issues LIST API calls to the kube-apiserver, especially high‑traffic controllers and CLI tools.
enrichment.fix: The APF configuration is updated to increase the maximum seats for LIST requests from the previous limit to 100, allowing more concurrent LIST operations before throttling occurs.
enrichment.impact: Clients that perform frequent or large LIST operations (e.g., controllers, kubectl, dashboards) experience reduced latency and fewer throttling errors, improving overall API server responsiveness and cluster usability.

feature.description: Graduated the WinOverlay feature in the kube-proxy to GA. The **WinOverlay** feature gate was enabled by default.
feature.author: rzlink
feature.userFacingChange: Graduate the WinOverlay feature in the kube-proxy to GA. The **WinOverlay** feature gate is now enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: The WinOverlay feature in kube-proxy was not enabled by default, requiring users to manually set the feature gate to use overlay networking on Windows nodes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that run Windows nodes with kube-proxy, especially those needing overlay networking (DSR) on Windows.
enrichment.fix: Graduated WinOverlay to GA and enabled the feature gate by default in kube-proxy, making overlay networking on Windows nodes automatically available.
enrichment.impact: Users no longer need to modify feature gates to get overlay support on Windows, reducing configuration complexity and ensuring stable, production‑ready networking for Windows workloads.

feature.description: Fixed recording the `kubelet_container_resize_requests_total` metric to include all resize-related updates.
feature.author: natasha41575
feature.userFacingChange: Fix recording the kubelet_container_resize_requests_total metric to include all resize-related updates.

enrichment.fix: The kubelet metric collection logic was updated to record every container resize-related update, ensuring all resize events are reflected in the `kubelet_container_resize_requests_total` metric.
enrichment.impact: Metrics consumers (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, alerting systems) now receive a correct count of container resize requests, improving monitoring accuracy and preventing false-negative alerts related to resource resizing on nodes.

feature.description: Promoted Windows graceful shutdown feature from alpha to beta.
feature.author: zylxjtu
feature.userFacingChange: It will promote windows graceful shutdown feature from alpha to beta.

enrichment.problem: Windows nodes only had an alpha‑stage graceful shutdown feature, limiting its stability and default usage for workloads that need proper termination handling.

feature.description:

feature.description: DRAAdminAccess was enabled by default allowing users to create `ResourceClaims` and `ResourceClaimTemplates` in privileged mode to grant access to devices that were in use by other users for admin tasks like monitoring health or status of the device.
feature.author: ritazh

enrichment.problem: Admin users could not create privileged ResourceClaims or ResourceClaimTemplates to access devices already in use by other workloads, making it hard to monitor device health or status without extra configuration.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use the Device Resource Allocation (DRA) APIs, particularly admin users needing to monitor or troubleshoot devices shared across workloads.

feature.description:

  - `scheduler_async_api_call_execution_total`: tracks executed API calls by call type and result (success/error)
  - `scheduler_async_api_call_duration_seconds`: histogram of API call execution duration by call type and result
  - `scheduler_pending_async_api_calls`: gauge showing current number of pending API calls in the queue.
feature.author: utam0k
feature.userFacingChange:
Added 3 new metrics for monitoring async API calls in the scheduler when the SchedulerAsyncAPICalls feature gate is enabled:
  - scheduler_async_api_call_execution_total: tracks executed API calls by call type and result (success/error)
  - scheduler_async_api_call_duration_seconds: histogram of API call execution duration by call type and result

feature.description: CRI API had auth fields in image pulling marked as `debug_redact`.
feature.author: SergeyKanzhelev

feature.description: Changed handling of `CustomResourceDefinitions` with unrecognized formats. Writing a schema with an unrecognized format now triggered a warning (the write was still accepted).

feature.description: Bumped `KubeletCgroupDriverFromCRI` to GA and add metric to track out-of-support CRI implementations.

feature.description: The scheduler no longer cleared the `nominatedNodeName` field for Pods. External components, such as Cluster Autoscaler and Karpenter, were responsible for managing this field when needed.

feature.description: Prevented any type of CPU/Memory alignment or hint generation with the Topology Manager from the CPU or Memory Manager when pod-level resources were used in the Pod spec.

issueContext.title: `AuthorizedTTL`, `UnauthorizedTTL` in `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1{alpha1,beta1}.AuthorizationConfiguration` cannot be set to `0`
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/16da2955d0ffeb7fcdfd7148ef2fb6c1ce1a9ef5/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/apis/apiserver/v1/types.go#L95-L104 suggests that the `AuthorizedTTL` and `UnauthorizedTTL` fields behave like the "legacy" `--authorization-webhook-cache-{un}authorized-ttl` flags. Yet, since they are no pointer types, they get defaulted if they are unset or explicitly set to `0` (which isn't the case when using the flags): https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/16da2955d0ffeb7fcdfd7148ef2fb6c1ce1a9ef5/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/apis/apiserver/v1/defaults.go#L52-L59

This prevents disabling caching, since setting it to `0` leads to defaulting. A workaround is to set a very low duration (`1ns` or similar), but it would be cleaner if the fields could simply be set to `0`.

Shouldn't we make them `*metav1.Duration` so that we can properly distinguish the cases where they are unset (and should be defaulted) and where they were explicitly set to `0`?

_Edit: Since this proposal is a breaking API change ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129237#issuecomment-2590367515)), another approach is [introducing dedicated fields](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129237#issuecomment-2591263513) for disabling caching explicitly._

### Why is this needed?

Prevent caching the decisions at all, similar to how it was possible before with setting

enrichment.problem: The AuthorizationConfiguration fields AuthorizedTTL and UnauthorizedTTL could not be set to zero, causing them to default and preventing users from completely disabling caching of webhook authorization decisions.
enrichment.affected: Any clusters using the kube-apiserver authorization webhook via the --authorization-config file that need to disable caching for authorized or unauthorized requests.
enrichment.fix: Introduced two new boolean fields, cacheAuthorizedRequests and cacheUnauthorizedRequests, in the --authorization-config file. Setting either field to false disables caching for authorized or unauthorized webhook requests respectively.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now opt‑out of caching authorization webhook decisions, ensuring every request is evaluated in real time when required (e.g., for security‑sensitive workloads). This provides finer‑grained control over auth performance vs. freshness without work‑arounds.
