apiChange.description: Zero-value `metadata.creationTimestamp` values are now omitted and no longer serialize an explicit `null` in JSON, YAML, and CBOR output
apiChange.author: liggitt

issueContext.title: Avoid serializing `creationTimestamp: null`
issueContext.body:
Context: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/67562#discussion_r211267314.

`creationTimestamp` is a struct (metav1.Time) right now:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/6d51311735705ecf30025df91216a82f397c9cfb/staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1/types.go#L175

However, it also has the `omitempty` json tag. The current behaviour at various places is to remove the field if it is an empty value.

From the [official docs](https://golang.org/pkg/encoding/json/#Marshal),

>  The "omitempty" option specifies that the field should be omitted from the encoding if the field has an empty value, defined as false, 0, a nil pointer, a nil interface value, and any empty array, slice, map, or string. 

This means that `omitempty` holds no meaning for structs. No matter what value `creationTimestamp` has, it should persist in the object. To truly adapt to it's intended behaviour, it should be a pointer (*time.Time), like `deletionTimestamp`. It also makes sense to have `creationTimestamp` as optional logically.

Right now, we don't allow an empty `creationTimestamp` to persist anyway, so it doesn't create a problem per se.

/sig api-machinery
/cc @sttts @liggitt @deads2k @lavalamp

enrichment.problem: Zero-value `metadata.creationTimestamp` fields were being serialized as explicit `null` in JSON, YAML, and CBOR output, leading to unnecessary fields in object representations.
enrichment.affected: All components that marshal Kubernetes objects (e.g., kube-apiserver, kubelet, kubectl, and any client libraries) will produce cleaner output without a `creationTimestamp: null` field when the timestamp is unset.
enrichment.fix: The serialization logic now treats zero-value `creationTimestamp` as omitted, so the field is not emitted at all when it has no value, removing the `null` entry from the output.
enrichment.impact: Reduces noise in resource manifests and API responses, improves readability, and prevents downstream tools from having to handle spurious `null` values for creation timestamps.

apiChange.description:
- Changed underlying logic to propagate pod-level hugepage cgroup to containers when they did not specify hugepage resources.
- Added validation to enforce the hugepage aggregated container limits to be smaller than or equal to pod-level limits. This was already enforced with the defaulted requests from the specified limits, however it did not make it clear about both hugepage requests and limits.
apiChange.author: KevinTMtz
apiChange.userFacingChange:
- Changes underlying logic to propagate Pod level hugepage cgroup to containers when they do not specify hugepage resources.
- Adds validation to enforce the hugepage aggregated container limits to be smaller or equal to pod-level limits. This was already enforced with the defaulted requests from the specified limits, however it did not make it clear about both hugepage requests and limits.

issueContext.title: Support for Pod-Level Hugepage Resources
issueContext.body:
Pod-Level Hugepage Resources was submitted in [[PodLevelResources] Pod Level Hugepage Resources](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130577).

New PR is required to propagate Pod level hugepage cgroup to containers.

enrichment.problem: When containers did not explicitly request hugepage resources, the pod‑level hugepage cgroup was not propagated to those containers, and the validation of aggregated hugepage limits vs. pod limits was unclear, allowing inconsistent resource enforcement.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use pod‑level hugepage resources, especially containers that do not declare their own hugepage requests or limits. Users relying on hugepages for databases, in‑memory caches, or other performance‑critical workloads are affected.
enrichment.fix: Updated the kubelet logic to always propagate the pod‑level hugepage cgroup to containers that lack their own hugepage specifications. Added stricter validation (in the API server) that ensures the sum of container hugepage limits does not exceed the pod‑level hugepage limits, covering both requests and limits.
enrichment.impact: Containers now correctly inherit pod‑level hugepage limits, preventing unexpected OOM or over‑allocation of hugepages and giving users clear error messages when limits are violated. This improves reliability for workloads that depend on hugepage memory.

apiChange.description:
Promoted feature-gate `VolumeAttributesClass` to GA
- Promoted API `VolumeAttributesClass` and `VolumeAttributesClassList` to `storage.k8s.io/v1`.
apiChange.author: carlory
apiChange.userFacingChange:
- Promoted feature-gate `VolumeAttributesClass` to GA
- Promoted API `VolumeAttributesClass` and `VolumeAttributesClassList` to `storage.k8s.io/v1`.

enrichment.problem: The VolumeAttributesClass API was only available as a beta feature behind the `VolumeAttributesClass` feature gate and the API objects lived in `storage.k8s.io/v1beta1`. Users had to enable the feature gate and use the beta version, which limited stability and prevented default usage in production workloads.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster that uses or plans to use the VolumeAttributesClass API (e.g., storage developers, CSI driver authors, and applications that rely on volume attribute classes) now gets a stable, default‑enabled API.
enrichment.fix: The `VolumeAttributesClass` feature gate has been promoted to GA and the API types `VolumeAttributesClass` and `VolumeAttributesClassList` have been moved to the stable `storage.k8s.io/v1` group version. The API is now enabled by default and supported as a stable storage API.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators and application developers can now use VolumeAttributesClass without extra feature‑gate configuration, and the API is guaranteed to be stable across releases. This simplifies storage class definitions, improves compatibility with CSI drivers, and encourages broader adoption of the feature.

apiChange.description:
The validation of `replicas` field in the ReplicationController `/scale` subresource has been migrated to declarative validation.
If the `DeclarativeValidation` feature gate is enabled, mismatches with existing validation are reported via metrics.
If the `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` feature gate is enabled, declarative validation is the primary source of errors for migrated fields.
apiChange.author: jpbetz
apiChange.userFacingChange:
The validation of `replicas` field in the ReplicationController `/scale` subresource has been migrated to declarative validation.
If the `DeclarativeValidation` feature gate is enabled, mismatches with existing validation are reported via metrics.
If the `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` feature gate is enabled, declarative validation is the primary source of errors for migrated fields.

enrichment.problem: The ReplicationController `/scale` subresource previously performed validation of the `replicas` field using legacy (imperative) validation code. This made validation behavior separate from the declarative validation framework and could lead to inconsistencies.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that uses a ReplicationController and performs scaling via the `/scale` subresource. Cluster administrators may see new validation metrics when the feature gates are enabled.
enrichment.fix: The validation logic for the `replicas` field has been migrated to the declarative validation system. When the `DeclarativeValidation` feature gate is on, any mismatches between the old and new validation are reported via metrics. Enabling `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` makes declarative validation the primary source of errors for the migrated field.
enrichment.impact: Validation becomes more consistent and observable. Users can monitor validation mismatches through metrics, and when the takeover gate is enabled, errors are reported directly from declarative validation, preparing the API for future cleanup and reducing duplicated validation code.

apiChange.description: kube-apiserver: the AuthenticationConfiguration type accepted in `--authentication-config` files has been promoted to `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1`.
apiChange.author: aramase

enrichment.problem: The AuthenticationConfiguration type used in `--authentication-config` files was only available in earlier (alpha/beta) API versions, preventing users from specifying a stable v1 configuration.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use `--authentication-config` to provide custom authentication configuration files; administrators managing API server authentication settings.
enrichment.fix: Promoted the AuthenticationConfiguration type to the stable `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1` version, allowing `--authentication-config` files to use the v1 API.
enrichment.impact: Cluster administrators can now define authentication configuration with a stable API version, improving long‑term compatibility and reducing the need for future migration work.

apiChange.description: kubectl: Graduated kuberc support to beta. A `kuberc` configuration file provided a mechanism for customizing `kubectl` behavior (distinct from kubeconfig, which configures cluster access across different clients).
apiChange.author: soltysh
apiChange.userFacingChange: kubectl: graduated `kuberc` support to beta. A `kuberc` configuration file provides a mechanism for customizing kubectl behavior (separate from kubeconfig, which configured cluster access across different clients).

enrichment.problem: kubectl's custom configuration file (kuberc) was only available as an alpha feature, making it unstable and unsuitable for production use, limiting users' ability to reliably customize kubectl behavior.
enrichment.affected: All kubectl users who want to customize client behavior via a kuberc file, especially those who previously avoided the alpha feature due to stability concerns.
enrichment.fix: The kuberc feature has been graduated to beta, providing a stable, supported configuration mechanism for customizing kubectl behavior separate from kubeconfig.
enrichment.impact: Users can now depend on kuberc for consistent client-side customizations (e.g., default flags, output formats) across environments, reducing the need for ad‑hoc scripts or wrappers and improving automation and usability of kubectl.

apiChange.description: kube-apiserver: Promoted the `StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration` feature gate to GA.
apiChange.author: aramase

enrichment.problem: Authentication configuration was only available via the experimental StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration feature gate, requiring manual enablement and lacking a stable API, which could lead to misconfigurations or incompatibilities for clusters that wanted to use it.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes clusters that configure authentication through the StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration API, especially those upgrading from older versions where the feature was gated.
enrichment.fix: The StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration feature gate has been promoted to GA in kube-apiserver, making the feature enabled by default and providing a stable, production‑ready API for authentication configuration.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now use structured authentication configuration out‑of‑the‑box without toggling a feature gate, benefiting from a stable, well‑supported API and reducing operational friction for secure authentication setups.

apiChange.description: DRA: Starting with Kubernetes 1.34, the alpha-level `resource.k8s.io/admin-access` label has been updated to `resource.kubernetes.io/admin-access`. Admins using the alpha feature and updating from 1.33 can set both labels, upgrade, then remove `resource.k8s.io/admin-access` when no downgrade is going to happen anymore.
apiChange.author: ritazh

enrichment.problem: The alpha `resource.k8s.io/admin-access` label used by the Device Resource Allocation (DRA) feature was renamed, causing clusters upgrading from 1.33 to 1.34 to lose the admin-access indication on resources if they only had the old label.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enabled the DRA alpha feature and used the `resource.k8s.io/admin-access` label on pods or other resources when upgrading from 1.33 to 1.34.
enrichment.fix: In Kubernetes 1.34 the label is renamed to `resource.kubernetes.io/admin-access`. The API server accepts both the old and new label during the transition, allowing admins to apply both labels, upgrade, and then drop the old one when no further downgrades are planned.
enrichment.impact: Prevents upgrade breakage for clusters using the DRA alpha feature. Admins can continue to use admin‑access semantics without manual resource recreation, ensuring a smooth upgrade path.

apiChange.description: DRA: The scheduler plugin prevented abnormal filter runtimes by timing out after 10 seconds. This was configurable via the plugin configuration's `FilterTimeout`. Setting it to zero disabled the timeout and restored the behavior of Kubernetes <= 1.33.
apiChange.author: pohly
apiChange.userFacingChange: DRA: the scheduler plugin now prevents abnormal filter runtimes by timing out after 10 seconds. This is configurable via the plugin configuration's `FilterTimeout`. Setting it to zero disables the timeout and restores the behavior of Kubernetes <= 1.33.

enrichment.problem: The DRA scheduler plugin could run filter functions for an unbounded amount of time, potentially hanging the scheduler and preventing pod placement.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the DRA scheduler plugin for pod placement could experience delayed or failed scheduling if a filter function hung.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a 10‑second timeout for filter execution in the DRA plugin. The timeout is configurable via the `FilterTimeout` field; setting it to zero disables the timeout and restores pre‑1.34 behavior.
enrichment.impact: Prevents scheduler stalls caused by long‑running DRA filter code, improving cluster stability and scheduling latency while still allowing operators to opt‑out if needed.

apiChange.description: Promoted the `RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation` feature gate to GA and locked it in the enabled state by default.
apiChange.author: HirazawaUi
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promote the RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation feature gate to GA and lock it in the default enabled state.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes only allowed a limited set of characters in container environment variable names, rejecting pods that used special characters. Users had to enable the RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation feature gate to work around this.
enrichment.affected: Any workload that sets environment variable names containing special characters (e.g., "_", "-", or other non‑alphanumeric symbols) and any cluster where the feature gate was previously disabled.
enrichment.fix: The RelaxedEnvironmentVariableValidation feature gate is promoted to GA and locked on (enabled) by default, allowing a broader set of characters in environment variable names without any additional configuration.
enrichment.impact: Pods that previously failed due to strict env‑var validation can now be created directly. No cluster‑wide configuration change is required, simplifying deployment of applications that rely on special characters in env‑var names.

apiChange.description: Promoted Job Pod Replacement Policy to general availability. The `JobPodReplacementPolicy` feature gate was locked to `true` and will be removed in a future Kubernetes release.
apiChange.author: dejanzele
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promoted Job Pod Replacement Policy to general availability. The `JobPodReplacementPolicy` feature gate is now locked to true, and will be removed in a future release of Kubernetes.

enrichment.problem: The JobPodReplacementPolicy feature was previously gated, requiring users to enable it to get automatic replacement of failed Job Pods. Users could also disable it, and some workflows depended on that ability.
enrichment.affected: Users and operators of Kubernetes Job resources (batch/v1) who previously relied on disabling the replacement policy, as well as any workloads that create Jobs.
enrichment.fix: The feature gate is now locked to true and promoted to General Availability. The Job controller will always enforce the pod replacement policy for Jobs, and the gate will be removed in a future release.
enrichment.impact: All clusters using Jobs will now have failed Pods automatically replaced without any configuration changes. Administrators can no longer opt‑out, simplifying the behavior but requiring awareness of the new default for existing workloads.

apiChange.description: The validation-gen code generator generated validation code that supported validation ratcheting.
apiChange.author: yongruilin
apiChange.userFacingChange: The validation-gen code generator generates validation code that supports validation ratcheting.

enrichment.problem: The validation‑gen code generator did not produce validation code that could perform validation ratcheting, making it difficult for API developers to evolve validation rules without breaking existing objects.
enrichment.affected: Developers writing API schemas or CRDs that rely on validation‑gen; clusters running APIs that use the generated validation code.
enrichment.fix: The generator now emits validation code that includes ratcheting support, allowing incremental changes to validation logic while preserving compatibility with previously stored resources.
enrichment.impact: API authors (including built‑in APIs and CRDs) can safely add or tighten validation rules without requiring disruptive migrations, improving API stability and reducing manual effort.

apiChange.description: Changed underlying logic for `Eviction Manager` helper functions.
apiChange.author: KevinTMtz
apiChange.userFacingChange: - No, changes underlying logic for Eviction Manager helper functions

issueContext.title: Add Support for Pod-Level Resources in eviction manager

enrichment.problem: Not specified - the change updates the internal helper functions used by the Eviction Manager, likely to improve correctness or enable future features.
enrichment.affected: Kubelet components that perform pod eviction; clusters using eviction manager behavior may see more reliable eviction handling.
enrichment.fix: Rewrites the underlying logic of the Eviction Manager helper functions, aligning them with upcoming support for pod‑level resources and improving internal behavior.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that eviction decisions made by the kubelet are based on more accurate logic, which can affect pod eviction handling and prepares the system for future enhancements such as pod‑level resource eviction.

apiChange.description: Promoted the `APIServerTracing` feature gate to GA. The `--tracing-config-file` flag accepted `TracingConfiguration` in version `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1` (with no changes from `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1`).
apiChange.author: dashpole
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promoted the `APIServerTracing` feature gate to GA. The `--tracing-config-file` flag now accepts `TracingConfiguration` in version `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1` (with no changes from `apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1`).

enrichment.problem: The `--tracing-config-file` flag only accepted `TracingConfiguration` in the beta API version (apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1beta1), preventing users from using a stable GA API version for configuring API server tracing.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the kube-apiserver `--tracing-config-file` flag for tracing configuration, especially during upgrades to newer Kubernetes versions.
enrichment.fix: The `APIServerTracing` feature gate was promoted to GA and the flag now accepts `TracingConfiguration` in the stable version apiserver.config.k8s.io/v1, with the same schema as the previous beta version.
enrichment.impact: Provides a stable, GA‑level API for configuring API server tracing, simplifying upgrades and ensuring consistent observability configuration across clusters.

apiChange.description: Promoted the `KubeletTracing` feature gate to GA.
apiChange.author: dashpole

enrichment.problem: Kubelet tracing was previously behind an experimental feature gate, requiring manual enablement and lacking GA guarantees.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes users running the kubelet who need tracing for observability; clusters that previously disabled the feature gate will now have tracing enabled by default.
enrichment.fix: The KubeletTracing feature gate has been promoted to GA, making tracing support in the kubelet stable and enabled by default in production clusters.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now reliably collect and export tracing data from the kubelet without additional configuration, improving observability for debugging and performance analysis.

apiChange.description: Promoted `MutableCSINodeAllocatableCount` to beta.
apiChange.author: torredil
apiChange.userFacingChange: Promote MutableCSINodeAllocatableCount to Beta.

enrichment.problem: CSINode allocatable resources were immutable, preventing administrators from dynamically adjusting CSI driver resource counts on nodes.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using CSI drivers that need to change node allocatable resources after node registration; storage administrators and automated provisioning tools.
enrichment.fix: The MutableCSINodeAllocatableCount feature is promoted to beta, allowing the CSINode.allocatable field to be mutated via the Kubernetes API.
enrichment.impact: Enables dynamic updates of CSI node resource capacities, improving storage provisioning flexibility and allowing production use of mutable allocatable counts.

apiChange.description: Introduced OpenAPI format support for `k8s-short-name` and `k8s-long-name` in CustomResourceDefinition schemas.
apiChange.author: jpbetz

enrichment.problem: CustomResourceDefinition OpenAPI schemas did not expose the `k8s-short-name` and `k8s-long-name` fields, so generated OpenAPI docs and tooling could not display or validate these naming conventions.
enrichment.affected: CRD authors and any clients or tools that consume the OpenAPI schema of a CustomResourceDefinition.
enrichment.fix: Added OpenAPI format support for `k8s-short-name` and `k8s-long-name` in CRD schemas, allowing these fields to be included in the OpenAPI v2/v3 output.
enrichment.impact: Improves developer experience and automation tools that rely on OpenAPI definitions (e.g., code generators, API discovery, validation), ensuring CRDs can fully describe short and long resource names.

apiChange.description:
- Added driver-owned fields in `ResourceSlice` to mark whether the device was shareable among multiple resource claims (or requests) and to specify how each capacity could be shared between different requests.
- Added user-owned fields in `ResourceClaim` to specify resource requirements against each device capacity.
- Added scheduler-owned field in `ResourceClaim.Status` to specify how much device capacity is reserved for a specific request.
- Added an additional identifier to `ResourceClaim.Status` for the device supports multiple allocations.
- Added a new constraint type to enforce uniqueness of specified attributes across all allocated devices.
apiChange.author: sunya-ch
apiChange.userFacingChange:
- Add driver-owned fields in ResourceSlice to mark whether the device is shareable among multiple resource claims (or requests) and to specify how each capacity can be shared between different requests.
- Add user-owned fields in ResourceClaim to specify resource requirements against each device capacity.
- Add scheduler-owned field in ResourceClaim.Status to specify how much device capacity is reserved for a specific request.
- Add an additional identifier to ResourceClaim.Status for the device supports multiple allocations.
- Add a new constraint type to enforce uniqueness of specified attributes across all allocated devices.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes lacked a way for device drivers to advertise shareable devices and for users to express per‑capacity requirements, making it impossible to safely share a single physical device across multiple ResourceClaims or to enforce uniqueness constraints on device attributes.
enrichment.affected: Cluster administrators, application developers, and device driver authors who need to allocate shared hardware resources such as GPUs, NICs, or accelerators.
enrichment.fix: Introduced new fields in the Device API: driver‑owned shareability flags and capacity‑sharing rules in ResourceSlice, user‑owned resource requirement fields in ResourceClaim, scheduler‑owned reservation fields in ResourceClaim.Status, an identifier for multi‑allocation devices, and a new constraint type to enforce attribute uniqueness across allocated devices.
enrichment.impact: Enables accurate scheduling of shared hardware devices, improves multi‑tenant device usage, and gives administrators fine‑grained control over device allocation, reducing contention and simplifying driver and scheduler integration.

apiChange.description: Allowed setting the `hostnameOverride` field in `PodSpec` to specify any RFC 1123 DNS subdomain as the pod's hostname. The `HostnameOverride` feature gate was introduced to control enablement of this functionality.
apiChange.author: HirazawaUi
apiChange.userFacingChange: Allows setting the `hostnameOverride` field in `PodSpec` to specify any RFC 1123 DNS subdomain as the pod's hostname. The `HostnameOverride` feature gate has been introduced to control enablement of this functionality.

enrichment.problem: Pods could not specify an arbitrary hostname; the hostname was derived from the pod name and limited to RFC 1123 subdomains, preventing workloads that require a specific DNS name from functioning correctly.
enrichment.affected: Any pod that needs a custom hostname, such as stateful applications, legacy services, or workloads that rely on specific DNS entries, especially when the default pod-name-derived hostname is insufficient.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a `hostnameOverride` field in `PodSpec` that allows users to set any RFC 1123 DNS subdomain as the pod’s hostname. Added the `HostnameOverride` feature gate to control the rollout of this capability.
enrichment.impact: Enables workloads that depend on a specific hostname or fully qualified domain name, improving compatibility with legacy applications and simplifying DNS-based service discovery. The feature can be toggled via a feature gate for gradual adoption.

apiChange.description: Updated the `v1` credential provider configuration to include the `tokenAttributes.cacheType` field. This field is required and must be set to either `ServiceAccount` or `Token` when configuring a provider that uses a service account to fetch registry credentials.
apiChange.author: aramase
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added `tokenAttributes.cacheType` field to v1 credential provider config. This field is required to be set to either ServiceAccount or Token when configuring a provider that uses service account to fetch registry credentials.

enrichment.problem: The v1 credential provider configuration did not include a required tokenAttributes.cacheType field, so providers that use a ServiceAccount to fetch registry credentials could be misconfigured and fail to obtain credentials, leading to image pull errors.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use a v1 image credential provider configured to fetch credentials via a service account and have not set tokenAttributes.cacheType.
enrichment.fix: Added the tokenAttributes.cacheType field to the v1 credential provider config schema and made it mandatory. Users must set it to either ServiceAccount or Token when configuring a provider that relies on a service account.
enrichment.impact: Credential providers can now correctly identify the cache type, preventing image pull failures caused by missing or incorrect configuration. Administrators need to update existing v1 credential provider configs to include the new field.

apiChange.description:
Added a new `FileKeyRef` field to containers, allowing them to load variables from files by setting this field.

Introduced the `EnvFiles` feature gate to govern activation of this functionality.
apiChange.author: HirazawaUi
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Add a new `FileKeyRef` field to containers, allowing them to load variables from files by setting this field.

Introduce the EnvFiles feature gate to govern activation of this functionality.

enrichment.problem: Containers could not directly load environment variable values from files, requiring manual handling via entrypoint scripts or volume mounts.
enrichment.affected: Users who need to set container environment variables from files, such as those using ConfigMaps, Secrets, or other volume‑mounted files.
enrichment.fix: Introduced a new `FileKeyRef` field in the container spec that references a file path to populate an environment variable. The functionality is gated behind the `EnvFiles` feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Simplifies configuration management by allowing pods to declare env vars sourced from files (e.g., ConfigMap or Secret volumes) without custom scripts, improving security and portability of workloads.

apiChange.description: Added a mechanism for configurable container restarts: _container-level restart rules_. This was an alpha feature behind the `ContainerRestartRules` feature gate.
apiChange.author: yuanwang04
apiChange.userFacingChange: Added a mechanism for configurable container restarts: _container level restart rules_. This is an alpha feature behind the `ContainerRestartRules` feature gate.

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes only supports pod-level restart policies, so all containers in a pod are restarted together. Users lacked a way to define per‑container restart behavior, leading to unnecessary restarts or inability to apply fine‑grained recovery logic.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that contain multiple containers in a pod and need distinct restart policies (e.g., sidecars, init containers, logging agents).
enrichment.fix: Introduced alpha container‑level restart rules behind the ContainerRestartRules feature gate. The API now accepts restart rules per container, and the kubelet respects these rules when handling container failures.
enrichment.impact: Operators can now configure restart behavior for individual containers, reducing disruption for multi‑container pods and enabling more precise fault‑handling strategies. This enhances workload reliability without requiring pod redesign.

apiChange.description: Promoted the `AuthorizeWithSelectors` and `AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors` feature gates to stable and locked on.
apiChange.author: liggitt
apiChange.userFacingChange: The `AuthorizeWithSelectors` and `AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors` feature gates are promoted to stable and locked on.

enrichment.problem: The AuthorizeWithSelectors and AuthorizeNodeWithSelectors authorization features were only available behind feature gates, requiring manual enablement and lacking guaranteed stability.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that want to use selector‑based authorization for pod or node access, and any workloads that depend on these authorizers.
enrichment.fix: Both feature gates have been promoted to GA (stable) and are now locked on, meaning they are always enabled without any configuration.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to enable these feature gates manually, simplifying setup and ensuring that selector‑based authorization is reliably available, improving security and consistency for workloads that rely on these authorizers.

apiChange.description: Dynamic Resource Allocation: Graduated core functionality to general availability (GA). This newly stable feature uses the _structured parameters_ flavor of DRA.
apiChange.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) was only available as an Alpha/experimental feature, so clusters could not rely on it for production workloads and lacked a stable API and implementation.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster that wants to use dynamic resource allocation for pods, especially those that depend on the DRA API or scheduler plugins, as well as administrators who previously avoided DRA due to its experimental status.
enrichment.fix: Graduated the core DRA functionality to General Availability (GA) and standardized on the structured‑parameters flavor, providing a stable API, default scheduling behavior, and full documentation.
enrichment.impact: Clusters can now safely use DRA in production to have the scheduler allocate resources dynamically based on workload requirements, improving resource utilization and enabling advanced placement scenarios without custom extensions.

apiChange.description: Added support for specifying `controlplane` or `cluster` egress selectors in JWT authenticators via the `issuer.egressSelectorType` field in the `AuthenticationConfiguration.jwt` array. If unset, the previous behavior of using no egress selector is preserved. This functionality requires the `StructuredAuthenticationConfigurationEgressSelector` beta feature gate (enabled by default).
apiChange.author: enj
apiChange.userFacingChange: JWT authenticators specified via the `AuthenticationConfiguration.jwt` array can now optionally specify either the `controlplane` or `cluster` egress selector by setting the `issuer.egressSelectorType` field.  When unset, the prior behavior of using no egress selector is retained.  The StructuredAuthenticationConfigurationEgressSelector beta feature (default on) must be enabled to use this functionality.

enrichment.problem: JWT authenticators could not be bound to a specific egress selector, forcing them to use the default (no selector) and limiting control over where token verification traffic is sent.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that configure JWT authenticators via AuthenticationConfiguration, especially those that need to direct authentication traffic to a specific egress path (control‑plane or cluster).
enrichment.fix: Adds an optional `issuer.egressSelectorType` field to `AuthenticationConfiguration.jwt` allowing users to select either `controlplane` or `cluster` egress selector. If the field is unset, the previous behavior (no egress selector) is retained. The beta feature gate `StructuredAuthenticationConfigurationEgressSelector` (enabled by default) must be on to use it.
enrichment.impact: Enables clusters to route JWT verification traffic through designated network paths, improving compliance with egress policies, supporting multi‑cluster or restricted‑network scenarios, and giving operators finer‑grained control over authentication traffic.

apiChange.description: Added support in the kubelet's image pull credential tracking for service account-based verification. When an image was pulled using service account credentials via external credential providers, subsequent Pods using the same service account (UID, name, and namespace) could access the cached image without re-authentication for the lifetime of that service account.
apiChange.author: aramase
apiChange.userFacingChange: The kubelet's image pull credential tracking now supports service account-based verification. When an image is pulled using service account credentials via external credential providers, subsequent pods using the same service account (UID, name, and namespace) can access the cached image without re-authentication for the lifetime of that service account.

enrichment.problem: When images were pulled using service account credentials via external credential providers, each pod using that service account had to re-authenticate, causing unnecessary credential lookups and latency.
enrichment.affected: Pods that use the same service account for image pulls on a node; nodes running the kubelet with external image credential providers.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now tracks image pull credentials per service account (UID, name, and namespace). After the first successful pull, subsequent pods that use the same service account can reuse the cached image without re‑authenticating for the lifetime of that service account.
enrichment.impact: Reduces authentication overhead and latency for workloads that rely on external image credential providers, improving node performance and lowering load on credential provider services.

apiChange.description:
Introduced the `admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1/MutatingAdmissionPolicy` API type. To enable, enable the `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` feature gate (which was off by default) and set `--runtime-config=admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1=true` on the kube-apiserver. 
Note that the default stored version remained alpha in 1.34, and whoever enabled beta during 1.34 needed to run a storage migration yourself to ensure you don't depend on alpha data in etcd.
apiChange.author: cici37
apiChange.userFacingChange:
Introduced the admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1/MutatingAdmissionPolicy API type.
To enable, enable the `MutatingAdmissionPolicy` feature gate (which is off by default) and set `--runtime-config=admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1=true` on the kube-apiserver. 
Note that the default stored version remains alpha in 1.34 and whoever enabled beta during 1.34 needs to run a storage migration yourself to ensure you don't depend on alpha data in etcd.

enrichment.problem: Clusters could only use the alpha MutatingAdmissionPolicy API version; a stable beta version was not available, and enabling the beta version without migrating stored data could leave workloads dependent on the alpha version in etcd.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that enable the MutatingAdmissionPolicy beta API (typically administrators) and any workloads that rely on MutatingAdmissionPolicy resources. Also impacts etcd data that stores the older alpha version.
enrichment.fix: Introduced the admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1 MutatingAdmissionPolicy API type. It can be enabled by turning on the MutatingAdmissionPolicy feature gate and adding --runtime-config=admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1beta1=true to the kube-apiserver. The default stored version remains alpha, so users must perform a manual storage migration when moving to beta.
enrichment.impact: Allows users to adopt the beta MutatingAdmissionPolicy API, giving a more stable contract than the alpha version. Administrators must be aware of and run a storage migration to avoid persisting alpha-format data, preventing potential incompatibilities in future upgrades.

apiChange.description:
The `conditionType` is "oneof" approved/denied check of CertificateSigningRequest's `.status.conditions` field was migrated to declarative validation. 
If the `DeclarativeValidation` feature gate was enabled, mismatches with existing validation are reported via metrics.
If the `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` feature gate was enabled, declarative validation was the primary source of errors for migrated fields.
apiChange.author: aaron-prindle
apiChange.userFacingChange:
The conditionType is "oneof" approved/denied check of CertificateSigningRequest's `.status.conditions` field has been migrated to declarative validation. 
If the `DeclarativeValidation` feature gate is enabled, mismatches with existing validation are reported via metrics.
If the `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` feature gate is enabled, declarative validation is the primary source of errors for migrated fields.

enrichment.problem: The oneof validation for the `conditionType` field of a CertificateSigningRequest's `.status.conditions` was implemented imperatively, leading to potential mismatches between runtime validation and the new declarative validation system.
enrichment.affected: Clients, controllers, and users that submit or approve/deny CertificateSigningRequests. The change is visible when the DeclarativeValidation feature gates are enabled.
enrichment.fix: The validation has been migrated to the declarative validation framework. When the `DeclarativeValidation` feature gate is on, any mismatches with the older validation are emitted as metrics. Enabling `DeclarativeValidationTakeover` makes the declarative validation the authoritative source of errors for this field.
enrichment.impact: Ensures consistency of CSR condition validation, provides observability of validation mismatches via metrics, and prepares the API for future validation improvements. Users and controllers that create or approve/deny CSRs will see validation errors from the new system when the feature gates are enabled.

apiChange.description: The `KubeletServiceAccountTokenForCredentialProviders` feature was beta and enabled by default.
apiChange.author: aramase
apiChange.userFacingChange: The KubeletServiceAccountTokenForCredentialProviders feature is now beta and enabled by default.

enrichment.problem: The KubeletServiceAccountTokenForCredentialProviders feature was previously gated (alpha or disabled by default), requiring manual enablement for workloads that rely on service account tokens for credential providers.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster running the kubelet that uses credential providers for pulling images or authenticating to external services; administrators no longer need to manually enable the feature gate.
enrichment.fix: The feature is promoted to beta and enabled by default in the kubelet, removing the need for explicit feature‑gate configuration.
enrichment.impact: Clusters no longer need to set the feature gate to use service account tokens with credential providers, simplifying configuration and enabling the functionality out‑of‑the‑box for all kubelet deployments.

documentation.description: `MultiCIDRServiceAllocator` was locked and enabled by default, `DisableAllocatorDualWrite` was enabled by default.
documentation.author: aojea
documentation.userFacingChange: MultiCIDRServiceAllocator is locked and enabled by default, DisableAllocatorDualWrite is enabled by default

documentation.description: Deprecated the `preferences` field in kubeconfig in favor of `kuberc`.
documentation.author: soltysh
documentation.userFacingChange: Deprecate preferences field in kubeconfig in favor of kuberc

deprecation.description: kubeadm: Exposed only the non-deprecated klog flags (-v and -vmodule), in line with KEP https://features.k8s.io/2845.
deprecation.author: carsontham
deprecation.userFacingChange: kubeadm: only expose non-deprecated klog flags, 'v' and 'vmodule', to align with KEP https://features.k8s.io/2845

enrichment.problem: kubeadm exposed deprecated klog command-line flags, causing potential confusion and future incompatibility for users relying on those flags.
enrichment.affected: Anyone using kubeadm to initialize or upgrade clusters who might have relied on deprecated logging flags such as -logtostderr, -stderrthreshold, etc.
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm binary now only exposes the non‑deprecated klog flags (-v and -vmodule), removing all other deprecated logging flags in line with KEP 2845.
enrichment.impact: Users gain a cleaner, future‑proof CLI; attempts to use removed flags will result in a clear error, reducing confusion and aligning kubeadm with the standardized logging interface used across the project.

issueContext.title: apimachinery/pkg/util/errors: deprecate MessageCountMap
issueContext.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Deprecate:
* [errors.MessageCountMap](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/errors#MessageCountMap)
* [errors.CreateAggregateFromMessageCountMap](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/errors#CreateAggregateFromMessageCountMap)

### Why is this needed?

* Not used anymore in the k8s.io codebase.
* Nobody should use the [`k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/errors`](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/errors) package anymore as [`errors.Join`](https://pkg.go.dev/errors#Join) exists since Go 1.20

enrichment.problem: The MessageCountMap type and CreateAggregateFromMessageCountMap function in the apimachinery errors package are no longer used in the Kubernetes codebase and have been superseded by the standard errors.Join introduced in Go 1.20.
enrichment.affected: Any external code or scripts that import k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/errors and use MessageCountMap or CreateAggregateFromMessageCountMap.
enrichment.fix: Both MessageCountMap and CreateAggregateFromMessageCountMap are marked as deprecated, signalling that they will be removed in a future release and encouraging users to switch to errors.Join.
enrichment.impact: Developers who currently depend on these APIs will receive deprecation warnings and need to migrate to errors.Join, simplifying error handling and reducing maintenance of unused code.
