bugOrRegression.description: Fixed SELinux warning controller not emitting events on some SELinux label conflicts.
bugOrRegression.author: jsafrane

enrichment.problem: The SELinux warning controller sometimes failed to emit events when SELinux label conflicts occurred, leaving users unaware of the conflict.
enrichment.affected: Users running SELinux‑enabled clusters, especially those troubleshooting pod SELinux label conflicts.
enrichment.fix: Added logic so the SELinux warning controller reliably creates events for all SELinux label conflict scenarios.
enrichment.impact: Clusters with SELinux enabled will now receive proper warning events for label conflicts, improving observability and troubleshooting of security label issues.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed broken shell completion for api resources.
bugOrRegression.author: vpnachev

enrichment.problem: kubectl shell auto-completion for API resources was broken, so commands like `kubectl get <TAB>` did not provide resource name suggestions.
enrichment.affected: Any user of kubectl who relies on shell auto‑completion for API resource names.
enrichment.fix: Restored correct generation of shell completion scripts for API resources, ensuring kubectl's completion works as expected.
enrichment.impact: Developers and administrators using shell completion regain accurate command suggestions, improving workflow efficiency and reducing errors.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: Fixed a 1.34 regression in CustomResourceDefinition handling that incorrectly warned about unrecognized formats on number and integer properties
bugOrRegression.author: yongruilin

enrichment.problem: kube-apiserver regression introduced in v1.34 caused it to emit warnings for CustomResourceDefinition schemas that used number or integer types with recognized formats, incorrectly treating them as unrecognized formats.
enrichment.affected: Anyone who defines CustomResourceDefinitions with number or integer properties, especially those relying on clean validation output.
enrichment.fix: The regression was corrected so that the apiserver no longer warns about valid number/integer formats in CRD schemas, restoring the original behavior.
enrichment.impact: Users creating or updating CRDs with numeric fields no longer see spurious warnings, reducing confusion and noise in logs and improving developer experience when defining custom resources.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: Fixes a 1.34 regression with spurious "Error getting keys" log messages
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes 1.34 introduced a regression in kube-apiserver that emitted spurious "Error getting keys" log messages, causing noisy logs and potential confusion during debugging.
enrichment.affected: All clusters running kube-apiserver version 1.34 experienced the noisy log messages.
enrichment.fix: The regression was fixed by correcting the error handling/path that generated the log, ensuring only genuine key‑retrieval errors are logged.
enrichment.impact: Reduces unnecessary log noise, making it easier for operators to spot real issues and preventing false alarms in monitoring systems.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: Fixes a possible 1.34 performance regression calculating object size statistics for resources not served from the watch cache, typically only Events
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: The apiserver could experience a performance regression when calculating object size statistics for resources that are not served from the watch cache, most commonly Event objects.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running the kube‑apiserver that rely on object size statistics, especially those with high Event traffic.
enrichment.fix: The kube‑apiserver code path that computes object size stats was corrected/optimized, eliminating the regression and restoring normal performance for non‑cached resources.
enrichment.impact: API server responsiveness is restored, preventing latency spikes for clusters that generate many Event objects or other non‑cached resources.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed bug where v1beta3's ClusterConfiguration.APIServer.TimeoutForControlPlane is not respected in newer versions of kubeadm where v1beta4 is the default.
bugOrRegression.author: HirazawaUi

enrichment.problem: When using kubeadm with a v1beta3 ClusterConfiguration, the APIServer.TimeoutForControlPlane setting was ignored in newer kubeadm releases where v1beta4 became the default configuration version, leading to unexpected control‑plane timeouts during init/upgrade.
enrichment.affected: Users of kubeadm who specified APIServer.TimeoutForControlPlane in a v1beta3 ClusterConfiguration, especially during upgrades to newer kubeadm versions where v1beta4 is default.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm was updated to correctly honor the TimeoutForControlPlane field from v1beta3 configurations even when v1beta4 is the default version, ensuring the timeout value is passed to the API server.
enrichment.impact: Clusters initialized or upgraded with kubeadm retain the intended control‑plane timeout behavior, preventing hangs or delays during control‑plane startup and improving overall reliability of the upgrade process.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.7
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes releases were built with an older Go compiler version, which can miss upstream Go security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source or using the released binaries; all core components compiled with the new Go version.
enrichment.fix: The build pipeline has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.24.7.
enrichment.impact: All clusters built from source or using binaries produced from this release benefit from the latest Go runtime security patches and performance enhancements, reducing the risk of compiler‑related issues and improving overall stability.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.9

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with an older Go version, missing recent Go security patches, bug fixes, and performance improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kubectl, kube-proxy, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: The build process has been updated to compile all Kubernetes components with Go 1.24.9.
enrichment.impact: All Kubernetes components now benefit from the latest Go runtime security updates and performance enhancements, reducing the risk of Go-related vulnerabilities and improving overall stability.

feature.description: update setcap and debian-base to bookworm-v1.0.6
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: The release build images were using outdated setcap binaries and an older Debian base, which could cause build failures or incompatibilities on newer Debian (bookworm) systems.
enrichment.affected: Developers, CI systems, and anyone building Kubernetes images from source that rely on the provided Debian build environment.
enrichment.fix: Updated the setcap package and switched the Debian base image to bookworm‑v1.0.6, ensuring builds use current libraries and OS components.
enrichment.impact: Build and CI pipelines that compile Kubernetes binaries now work reliably on the latest Debian release, reducing build‑time errors for developers and downstream packagers.

bugOrRegression.description: Bump system-validators to v1.10.2: remove version-specific cgroup kernel config checks to avoid false failures on cgroup v2 systems when v1-only configs are missing.
bugOrRegression.author: pacoxu

enrichment.problem: System validators performed version‑specific kernel configuration checks for cgroup v1, causing false validation failures on nodes that use cgroup v2 when the v1‑only configs are absent.
enrichment.affected: Clusters with nodes using cgroup v2 where the kubelet’s system‑validator would previously flag missing cgroup‑v1 kernel configs, leading to false node health failures.
enrichment.fix: Updated system‑validators to v1.10.2 and removed the cgroup‑v1 specific kernel config checks, so validation no longer expects those settings on cgroup v2 systems.
enrichment.impact: Nodes running with cgroup v2 can now start and join the cluster without spurious errors, preventing unnecessary node re‑boots or cluster‑wide disruptions during upgrades.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix Windows kube-proxy (winkernel) issue where stale RemoteEndpoints remained
  when a Deployment was referenced by multiple Services due to premature clearing
  of the terminatedEndpoints map.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes using the winkernel kube-proxy, stale RemoteEndpoints were left behind when a Deployment was referenced by multiple Services. The termination logic cleared the terminatedEndpoints map too early, causing old endpoint entries to persist.
enrichment.affected: Users running Windows nodes with kube-proxy (winkernel) where a Deployment is targeted by multiple Services. Stale endpoints could cause traffic to be sent to non‑existent pods.
enrichment.fix: The kube-proxy code now delays clearing of the terminatedEndpoints map until all Services referencing the Deployment have been processed, ensuring RemoteEndpoints are correctly removed.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads that expose a Deployment via more than one Service will see correct traffic routing and no accidental routing to terminated pods, improving reliability of network traffic on Windows clusters.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix Windows kube-proxy to prevent intermittent deletion of ClusterIP load balancers in HNS when internalTrafficPolicy=Local, ensuring stable service connectivity.
bugOrRegression.author: princepereira

enrichment.problem: On Windows nodes, kube-proxy could intermittently delete ClusterIP load balancers in HNS when a Service has internalTrafficPolicy=Local, causing loss of service connectivity.
enrichment.affected: Windows nodes running kube-proxy with Services that use internalTrafficPolicy=Local and a ClusterIP; any pods behind those services could experience connectivity loss.
enrichment.fix: The Windows kube-proxy implementation was updated to retain the HNS load balancer for ClusterIP services when internalTrafficPolicy is set to Local, eliminating the unintended deletions.
enrichment.impact: Windows workloads that rely on ClusterIP services with internalTrafficPolicy=Local now have stable, uninterrupted network connectivity, preventing unexpected service outages.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix missing kubelet_volume_stats_* metrics
bugOrRegression.author: huww98

enrichment.problem: The kubelet failed to expose the kubelet_volume_stats_* metrics, so volume usage statistics were missing from Prometheus and other monitoring systems.
enrichment.affected: Clusters where workloads rely on kubelet_volume_stats metrics for storage monitoring; monitoring stacks like Prometheus that scrape kubelet metrics were missing volume stats.
enrichment.fix: Implemented the missing metric collection and exposition in the kubelet, ensuring that kubelet_volume_stats_* metrics are now emitted correctly.
enrichment.impact: Users can now monitor per‑volume resource usage (capacity, used bytes, inodes, etc.) via standard metrics pipelines, improving observability and enabling proper alerting on storage pressure.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix panic on kubectl api-resources
bugOrRegression.author: rikatz

enrichment.problem: kubectl crashes with a panic when the user runs the `kubectl api-resources` command.
enrichment.affected: All users of the kubectl CLI who invoke `kubectl api-resources`, regardless of cluster version.
enrichment.fix: Added proper checks and handling in the kubectl code path for `api-resources` to prevent the panic, ensuring the command completes successfully.
enrichment.impact: Users can safely list API resources with kubectl again, restoring a core CLI functionality needed for discovery and scripting.

bugOrRegression.description:
Fix the bug which could result in Job status updates failing with the error:
  status.startTime: Required value: startTime cannot be removed for unsuspended job
  The error could be raised after a Job is resumed, if started and suspended previously.
bugOrRegression.author: dejanzele

enrichment.problem: When a Job that had been started and then suspended was later resumed, the Job controller could attempt to update the Job status and be rejected with the validation error: "status.startTime: Required value: startTime cannot be removed for unsuspended job". This prevented the Job status from being updated.
enrichment.affected: Users running batch Jobs that suspend and later resume them. The issue manifested as failed status updates and potentially incorrect Job phase reporting.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the Job controller (and related validation logic) to retain the startTime field when a suspended Job is resumed, allowing the status update to succeed.
enrichment.impact: Jobs that use the suspend/resume feature can now correctly update their status after being resumed, preventing jobs from appearing stuck or failed due to a validation error.

bugOrRegression.description: Fix: The requests for a config FromClass in the status of a ResourceClaim were not referenced.
bugOrRegression.author: LionelJouin

enrichment.problem: When a ResourceClaim specified a config via configFromClass, the resulting resource requests were not recorded in the claim's status, so the requests were effectively ignored.
enrichment.affected: Users creating ResourceClaims that use configFromClass (and the pods that depend on those claims).
enrichment.fix: The controller now correctly copies the requests derived from configFromClass into the ResourceClaim status, ensuring they are referenced during scheduling and allocation.
enrichment.impact: Pods that use a ResourceClaim with configFromClass will receive the correct resource requests, preventing scheduling failures or silent resource mismatches.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug in kube-proxy nftables mode (GA as of 1.33) that fails to determine if traffic originates from a local source on the node. The issue was caused by using the wrong meta `iif` instead of `iifname` for name based matches.
bugOrRegression.author: jack4it

enrichment.problem: kube-proxy in nftables mode used the wrong nftables meta field (iif) for name‑based matches, causing it to fail to recognise traffic that originates from the local node. This could lead to incorrect routing or dropping of local service traffic.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-proxy with nftables mode, particularly workloads that rely on correct local‑source traffic handling such as Services and NetworkPolicies.
enrichment.fix: The nftables rule generation was updated to use the proper meta field `iifname` for name‑based matches, ensuring correct identification of locally‑sourced traffic.
enrichment.impact: Local traffic is now correctly identified and proxied, restoring proper service load‑balancing and network‑policy enforcement for clusters using kube-proxy's nftables mode (GA in 1.33).

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a bug in kube-scheduler where pending pod preemption caused preemptor pods to be retried more frequently.
bugOrRegression.author: macsko

enrichment.problem: When a pending pod triggered preemption, kube-scheduler mistakenly retried the preemptor pods more frequently than needed, causing unnecessary scheduling attempts.
enrichment.affected: Pods that rely on preemption (using priority classes) and clusters where preemption occurs.
enrichment.fix: The scheduler code was corrected to properly handle pending pod preemption, stopping the extra retries of preemptor pods.
enrichment.impact: Reduces wasted scheduler cycles and CPU usage, leading to faster scheduling of high‑priority pods and overall more efficient cluster operation.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixed a startup probe race condition that caused main containers to remain stuck in "Initializing" state when sidecar containers with startup probes failed initially but succeeded on restart in pods with restartPolicy=Never.
bugOrRegression.author: yuanwang04

enrichment.problem: A race condition between a sidecar container's startup probe and the main container caused the main container to remain in the "Initializing" phase, preventing the pod from becoming Ready. This occurred when the sidecar's startup probe initially failed but later succeeded after a restart, in pods with restartPolicy=Never.
enrichment.affected: Workloads that include sidecar containers with startup probes and set restartPolicy=Never (e.g., service mesh sidecars, logging or security sidecars).
enrichment.fix: The kubelet's handling of startup probes was updated to correctly synchronize the state of sidecar containers with the main container, eliminating the race condition so that the main container can transition out of the Initializing state once the sidecar’s startup probe succeeds.
enrichment.impact: Pods that rely on sidecars with startup probes and use restartPolicy=Never no longer get stuck in the Initializing state, improving reliability and ensuring workload availability without manual intervention.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-controller-manager: Fixes a 1.34 regression, which triggered a spurious rollout of existing statefulsets when upgrading the control plane from 1.33 → 1.34. This fix is guarded by a `StatefulSetSemanticRevisionComparison` feature gate, which is enabled by default.
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: Upgrading the control plane from Kubernetes 1.33 to 1.34 triggered a regression in kube-controller-manager that incorrectly compared StatefulSet revisions, causing a spurious rollout (restart) of existing StatefulSets.
enrichment.affected: Any cluster performing a control‑plane upgrade from v1.33 to v1.34 that runs StatefulSets. The issue primarily affected workloads managed by StatefulSets, causing them to be redeployed unnecessarily.
enrichment.fix: The revision‑comparison logic in kube-controller-manager was corrected. The change is protected by the `StatefulSetSemanticRevisionComparison` feature gate, which is now enabled by default, preventing unintended rollouts during upgrades.
enrichment.impact: Clusters upgrading to 1.34 will no longer experience unnecessary StatefulSet rollouts, avoiding unintended pod restarts, potential disruption, and extra workload on the cluster during upgrades.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-controller-manager: Resolves potential issues handling pods with incorrect uids in their ownerReference
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: The controller manager could mishandle pods whose ownerReference contained an incorrect UID, leading to failures in controller operations such as garbage collection, adoption, or deletion of those pods.
enrichment.affected: Any workload controller that interacts with pod ownerReferences, such as Deployments, ReplicaSets, and StatefulSets, could be impacted when pods have malformed ownerReference UIDs.
enrichment.fix: Added validation and corrected handling of ownerReference UIDs in the kube-controller-manager so that pods with mismatched or missing UIDs are processed safely without causing controller errors.
enrichment.impact: Controllers (e.g., ReplicaSet, Deployment, StatefulSet) can now reliably manage pods even when the ownerReference UID is wrong, preventing orphaned or stuck pods and improving cluster stability.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-scheduler: Pod statuses no longer include specific taint keys or values when scheduling fails because of untolerated taints
bugOrRegression.author: hoskeri

enrichment.problem: When a pod could not be scheduled due to untolerated node taints, the pod status included the exact taint key and value, exposing detailed node taint information in the pod’s condition.
enrichment.affected: Users who inspect pod status for scheduling failures will see less detailed information about the offending taints. The change only affects the scheduler's reporting behavior.
enrichment.fix: Kube‑scheduler now omits the specific taint key/value from the pod’s status when scheduling fails because of an untolerated taint. The failure reason is still reported, but without revealing the taint details.
enrichment.impact: Pod status messages become less noisy and do not leak node taint specifics, improving clarity and security. Users must look at scheduler events or logs for the full taint information when debugging scheduling failures.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: avoid panicing if the user has malformed the kubeconfig in the cluster-info config map to not include a valid current context. Include proper validation at the appropriate locations and throw errors instead.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: kubeadm would panic when the kubeconfig stored in the cluster-info ConfigMap lacked a valid current-context, causing the command to crash instead of reporting a clear error.
enrichment.affected: Users running kubeadm commands (e.g., init, join, upgrade) on clusters where the cluster-info ConfigMap contains an invalid kubeconfig.
enrichment.fix: Added validation checks in the relevant kubeadm code paths to detect a missing or malformed current-context in the ConfigMap's kubeconfig and return an informative error rather than panicking.
enrichment.impact: Prevents kubeadm crashes during init/join or upgrade operations, giving operators a readable error message and improving overall reliability of cluster lifecycle tooling.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: ensured waiting for apiserver uses a local client that doesn't reach to the control plane endpoint and instead reaches directly to the local API server endpoint.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: During kubeadm init/join, the wait loop for the API server used a client that contacted the advertised control‑plane endpoint. If that endpoint was unreachable (e.g., DNS issues, load‑balancer problems), kubeadm could timeout or fail even though the local API server was already ready.
enrichment.affected: Users running `kubeadm init` or `kubeadm join` to bring up control‑plane nodes, especially in environments with external load balancers or DNS delays.
enrichment.fix: kubeadm now creates a local client that connects directly to the local API server endpoint (localhost) while waiting for the API server to become healthy, bypassing the external control‑plane address.
enrichment.impact: Improves reliability and speed of cluster bootstrapping with kubeadm. Users no longer experience false‑negative health checks or hangs when the control‑plane endpoint is temporarily unreachable, leading to smoother cluster creation and node joins.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixed a bug where the node registration information for a given node was not fetched correctly during "kubeadm upgrade node" and the node name can end up being incorrect in cases where the node name is not the same as the host name.
bugOrRegression.author: neolit123

enrichment.problem: During `kubeadm upgrade node`, kubeadm failed to fetch the node registration information correctly, causing the node name to be overwritten with the hostname when the node's name did not match the host name.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using `kubeadm upgrade node` on nodes whose Kubernetes node name is different from the host's name.
enrichment.fix: The upgrade process now correctly retrieves the node registration data, preserving the original node name even when it differs from the machine's hostname.
enrichment.impact: Keeps node identity stable during upgrades, avoiding potential scheduling, monitoring, or networking issues caused by an unexpected node name change.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: fixes a preflight check that can fail hostname construction in IPV6 setups
bugOrRegression.author: liggitt

enrichment.problem: The kubeadm preflight check that validates the node hostname could fail when constructing the hostname on IPv6-only networks, causing kubeadm init/join to abort.
enrichment.affected: Users attempting to create or join clusters on IPv6 networks using kubeadm were unable to complete the bootstrap process.
enrichment.fix: The hostname construction logic in the preflight validator was corrected to handle IPv6 addresses properly, allowing the check to succeed on IPv6 setups.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that use IPv6 can now be bootstrapped with kubeadm without encountering hostname‑related preflight failures, reducing setup friction and avoiding unnecessary rollbacks.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubelet: the connection to a DRA driver became unusable because of an internal deadlock when a connection was idle for 30 minutes.
bugOrRegression.author: pohly

enrichment.problem: Kubelet’s connection to a Device Resource Allocation (DRA) driver could deadlock and become unusable after being idle for 30 minutes, breaking communication with the driver.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using DRA drivers on nodes; any pods that rely on device resource allocation through DRA.
enrichment.fix: The Kubelet’s internal locking around the DRA driver connection was corrected to prevent the deadlock, ensuring the connection remains functional even after long idle periods.
enrichment.impact: Restores reliable operation of DRA drivers on nodes, preventing node‑level resource allocation failures for workloads that depend on device resources (e.g., GPUs, specialized hardware).

bugOrRegression.description: Reduce event spam during volume operation errors in Portworx in-tree driver
bugOrRegression.author: gohilankit

enrichment.problem: When a volume operation fails in the Portworx in‑tree driver, it generates a large number of Kubernetes events, creating event spam.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use the Portworx in‑tree volume driver; users who previously saw many repetitive error events during volume operation failures.
enrichment.fix: The driver now throttles or de‑duplicates error events, dramatically reducing the number of events emitted for a single volume operation failure.
enrichment.impact: Reduces noise in `kubectl get events` and downstream monitoring, making real problems easier to spot and lowering API‑server/event handling load for clusters using the Portworx in‑tree driver.

bugOrRegression.description: Remove incorrectly printed warning for SessionAffinity whenever a headless service is creater or updated
bugOrRegression.author: Peac36

enrichment.problem: A warning about SessionAffinity was printed incorrectly whenever a headless Service was created or updated, causing confusion for users.
enrichment.affected: Users creating or updating headless Services observed an inaccurate SessionAffinity warning.
enrichment.fix: The spurious warning has been removed, so creating or updating headless Services no longer emits an incorrect SessionAffinity warning.
enrichment.impact: Eliminates noisy, misleading output for users managing headless Services, improving the user experience and preventing unnecessary troubleshooting.

bugOrRegression.description: The SchedulerAsyncAPICalls feature gate has been disabled to mitigate a bug where its interaction with asynchronous preemption in could degrade kube-scheduler performance, particularly under high kube-apiserver load.
bugOrRegression.author: macsko

enrichment.problem: When the SchedulerAsyncAPICalls feature gate was enabled, its interaction with asynchronous preemption could cause the kube-scheduler to experience significant performance degradation, especially under high kube-apiserver load.
enrichment.affected: Clusters using the SchedulerAsyncAPICalls feature gate, particularly those with high apiserver traffic, experienced degraded scheduling latency.
enrichment.fix: The SchedulerAsyncAPICalls feature gate has been disabled by default, preventing the problematic interaction and restoring normal scheduler performance.
enrichment.impact: Clusters that had the feature gate enabled will no longer see scheduler slowdowns under load, but the async API call functionality is temporarily unavailable until the bug is resolved.

other.description: Kubeadm: updated the supported etcd version to v3.5.24 for the skewed control plane version v1.33.
other.author: joshjms

enrichment.problem: kubeadm did not list etcd v3.5.24 as a supported version for the skewed control‑plane version v1.33, leading to potential compatibility warnings or failures when users tried to use that etcd version.
enrichment.affected: Anyone running kubeadm to create or join a cluster with control‑plane version v1.33 who wants to use etcd v3.5.24.
enrichment.fix: The kubeadm version‑skew matrix was updated to include etcd v3.5.24 as a supported etcd version for control‑plane v1.33.
enrichment.impact: Users can now initialise or join clusters with kubeadm using etcd v3.5.24 and control‑plane v1.33 without compatibility issues, simplifying upgrades and new deployments.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.10
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were still being built with an older Go version, which could miss upstream Go security patches, bug fixes, and compatibility improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes components (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) that are compiled from source.
enrichment.fix: The build pipeline has been updated to use Go 1.24.10 for compiling all Kubernetes components.
enrichment.impact: Ensures that all Kubernetes binaries benefit from the latest Go runtime security patches and performance improvements, reducing supply‑chain risk and improving build reliability. No functional changes for users.

feature.description: Kubernetes is now built using Go 1.24.11
feature.author: cpanato

enrichment.problem: Kubernetes binaries were previously built with older Go version, lacking recent Go security patches and improvements.
enrichment.affected: All Kubernetes binaries (kube-apiserver, kube-scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, etc.) are rebuilt with the newer Go version.
enrichment.fix: All Kubernetes components are now compiled with Go 1.24.11, updating the toolchain used for building the release.
enrichment.impact: Provides security and performance improvements from the newer Go runtime, reduces exposure to Go-related vulnerabilities, and ensures compatibility with future Go ecosystem updates.

bugOrRegression.description: Fixes a spurious "namespace not found" error possible in default configurations in 1.30+ when using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or MutatingAdmissionPolicy to intercept namespaced objects in newly-created namespaces
bugOrRegression.author: lalitc375

enrichment.problem: When using ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or MutatingAdmissionPolicy to intercept namespaced objects in newly‑created namespaces, the API server could return a spurious "namespace not found" error under default configurations in Kubernetes 1.30+.
enrichment.affected: Clusters that use ValidatingAdmissionPolicy or MutatingAdmissionPolicy to validate or mutate resources in namespaces that are created shortly before the resource creation.
enrichment.fix: Adjusted the admission policy handling logic so that newly‑created namespaces are correctly recognized, eliminating the false "namespace not found" error for both validating and mutating admission policies.
enrichment.impact: Users employing admission policies no longer see unexpected namespace lookup failures, allowing workloads to be created and validated reliably in freshly created namespaces.

bugOrRegression.description: K8s.io/client-go: Fixes a regression in 1.34+ which prevented informers from using configured Transformer functions
bugOrRegression.author: serathius

enrichment.problem: In Kubernetes 1.34 and later, informers in the client-go library stopped applying configured Transformer functions, causing objects to be delivered to event handlers without the expected transformations.
enrichment.affected: Go applications using client-go informers with custom Transformer functions (e.g., controllers, operators) were receiving untransformed objects.
enrichment.fix: Restores the proper execution of configured Transformer functions in informers, re‑enabling the transformation step that was unintentionally disabled by the regression.
enrichment.impact: Controllers, operators, and any Go applications that rely on client-go informers with custom Transformers regain correct behavior, preventing subtle bugs and data inconsistencies in watch handling.

bugOrRegression.description: Kube-apiserver: Fixes spurious warning log messages about enabled alpha APIs while starting API server
bugOrRegression.author: michaelasp

enrichment.problem: Kube-apiserver emitted spurious warning log messages about enabled alpha APIs during startup, causing confusing and unnecessary warnings in logs.
enrichment.affected: Clusters running kube-apiserver, especially those with alpha APIs disabled or not explicitly enabled, experienced misleading warning logs.
enrichment.fix: The startup code now correctly detects when alpha APIs are not actually enabled and suppresses the erroneous warning messages.
enrichment.impact: Admins and operators see cleaner logs without misleading warnings, simplifying troubleshooting and reducing log noise.

bugOrRegression.description: Kubeadm: unhide the "etcd-join" phase of "kubeadm join" to allow on-demand execution of the phase if the ControlPlaneLocalMode feature gate is not enabled
bugOrRegression.author: borovetsav

enrichment.problem: The "etcd-join" phase of the "kubeadm join" command was hidden, preventing administrators from manually executing the phase to add or replace etcd members when the ControlPlaneLocalMode feature gate was not enabled.
enrichment.affected: Administrators using kubeadm to join nodes or manage etcd members in clusters where ControlPlaneLocalMode is disabled.
enrichment.fix: The "etcd-join" phase is now unhidden and exposed as an on‑demand sub‑command of "kubeadm join", allowing users to run it directly without needing the ControlPlaneLocalMode feature gate.
enrichment.impact: Cluster operators can now add or recover etcd members using kubeadm without changing feature‑gate settings, simplifying cluster upgrades, recovery, and scaling of the etcd cluster.

bugOrRegression.description: Make / build: fix docker IP address detection
bugOrRegression.author: BenTheElder

enrichment.problem: The build system failed to correctly detect the Docker daemon's IP address, causing build scripts that rely on Docker networking to break in certain environments.
enrichment.affected: Anyone building Kubernetes from source, especially CI environments that run Docker locally.
enrichment.fix: Updated the Makefile/build scripts to improve Docker IP address detection logic, ensuring reliable identification of the Docker host address across common setups.
enrichment.impact: Developers and CI pipelines can now build Kubernetes binaries without Docker IP detection errors, reducing build failures and improving reliability of automated testing.

bugOrRegression.description: The slow initialization of container runtime will not cause System WatchDog to kill kubelet. Device Manager is not considered healthy before it attempted to start listening on the port.
bugOrRegression.author: SergeyKanzhelev

enrichment.problem: A slow container runtime initialization triggered the System WatchDog to kill the kubelet, and the Device Manager was incorrectly marked healthy before it started listening on its port.
enrichment.affected: Nodes running kubelet with slow container runtime startup or device plugins; the kubelet process and its Device Manager component are directly impacted.
enrichment.fix: The kubelet now excludes slow CRI initialization from WatchDog kill criteria, and the Device Manager health check is updated to report healthy only after it successfully begins listening on its port.
enrichment.impact: Nodes remain operational even when the container runtime starts slowly, and Device Manager health reporting is accurate, preventing premature node health false‑positives and reducing unexpected kubelet restarts.
